It took about 5 minutes if that. He didn’t tell us anything more than was written up on a placard by each tank. We had to go back to read each one ourselves. We have visited other hatcheries in SriLanka where we have been given much more information.
Great place to visit the owner was so good at explaining what they do and how they are saving the turtles.... Highly recommended you visit this place

Great way to learn about the different types of Turtles etc. and that they are doing their bit to assist in their survival. Our Guide was extremely dedicated, perhaps a little too dedicated and had trouble excepting jokes! None the less the orphanage side for sick or injured Turtles is an important part of their role.

It is worth a visit as quite interesting but I do feel they need to give the Turtles deeper and bigger tanks.  Our guide was very evasive when asked about what they did with the week old turtles and when or how they were released.  Cost 500 rupees each to enter.  It is helping preserve the endangered turtles though

A great place to learn and experience what we all need to do to protect these wild animals. You can learn a lot from the people who work here. Plus you can see some wild turtles being rehabilitated after being caught in fishing nets and have some really nasty injuries. If there are some baby turtles in there then you can set them free in the evening. Which is great for all ages. It's not to expensive so go and learn something and have a great day there.

We were not expecting too much according to TA reviews, but at the end it was very pleasant experience. These people are doing really lot for saving all kinds of sea turtles and also very important job in educating kids to protect the turtles and wildlife generally. If you want to see releasing of freshly born turtle babies into the see in the evening, you have to call in advance and manage your coming with the staff. No extra charge for that. Only negative is already mentioned small living space for resident older turtles. After so many years they could finally make pools bigger. Entrance fee is 500 Rp, but I think it is a good idea to put some extra in donation box, as we did.
Entry was LKR 500. Spent some 15 mins there. New post experience. Played with turtles and took some photos. Awesome.
Visited hatchery hikkaduwa on recommendation of our driver its not  worth of money but can be a good contribution for a noble cause saving handicapped turtles 👍👍

It seems they believe providing protective hatchery will increase the number of turtle. Not really a professional protective project. Per person, it costs 1,000 rupees. They explained many time why they receive costly entrance fee. All will be used maintain their (turtle and people there) life.
" Very nice " " Great place to visit ." " One of the best turtle hatchery in sri lanka. " " great experience ”

No doubt the turtles a cute, though the conditions of the "Sanctuary" are very poor. Some of the bigger turtles are "imprisoned" with barely enough room to turn around. They claim they have this place to care of the turtles; if so they need to improve the living conditions and facilities of their inhabitants.

Totally not worth the visit.  This place is very small and staff totally unfriendly.  The man gave us tickets and told us to walk around ourselves....and rudely warned that we could pick up the baby turtles only once! There was another foreign older couple who arrived after us as we were finishing off our viewing of the turtles...and the manager gave them a briefing/tour!!  Btw, when we were there...we were the only people who were visiting at that time...discrimation! We were staying at Heritance Ahungalla  and they promote Kosgoda Sea Turtle Conservation Project...I have been to that one and there is such a HUGE difference!! Foreigners are charged Rs500, locals/residents - free
Good for bringing awareness to a layman about importance of conservation of Turtles. Appreciate the efforts of Mr. Chaminda and his team.
We were happy to see that turtles are taken care of. We saw some poor handicapped turtles but glad they are in good hands. We hope the managers can build deeper tanks for turtles one day.
Absolutely amazing experience, they are doing such great work. Volunteers were there from all over the world to help with turtle feeding
This visit not what I expected small sand hatchery, several tanks with damaged turtles in due to collision with motor boats. Visit lasted minutes worth visit but not up to much.

After some debate over whether we should we decided to visit and see for ourselves. In the context of the local situation this Hatchery is doing a lot of good work. They are trying to educate local people against eating turtle eggs and turtle soup, caring for injured turtles and trying to release those that can back into the wild. They are also protecting a lot of eggs that would otherwise be sold or eaten by other wildlife, (although the practice of moving eggs for safe keeping is debatable.) The staff come across as genuinely caring for the turtles and their personal story is moving. Sadly we visited at the same time as a local school/youth group and it was sad to see the disregard the local children had for the turtles. They were picking them up aggressively out of the water as soon as the teacher's head was turned. The staff were genuinely trying to stop this happening but were completely overwhelmed. At the end of our visit the staff said there was one turtle that is comfortable to be picked up (for photo etc,) but we decided to decline the offer. We were very happy getting up close to these creatures and didn't feel the need. You can choose not to touch them!!! Overall I would recommend visiting but perhaps we can improve the hatchery by highlighting these negative aspects.
The team were so informative and provided a great experience. I would highly recommend doing this experience.

Loved this place. Doing really good work to help turtles. You are allowed to handle some of them which at first I wasn't sure about but they all have to be handled daily anyway when their water is changed and tank cleaned. All turtles that can be released are and this place is very educational.

Well worth the trip in - cheap entry fee.  Worthy cause to donate some of the money that you've saved from eating at cheap restaurants. Reminder at the beginning of the total devastation of the December 26, 2004 tsunami - rebuilt and still continuing the effort of rehabilitating older turtles that had been damaged as well as rescuing turtle eggs dug up by locals to eating purposes. Please consider leaving a donation for this very worthy cause.

Visited this place when we are on our way back to the city, and even its midday the variety of turtles was introduced to us and some of the baby turtles are waiting for sunset for their release to the sea but unfortunately, we couldn't stay longer to witness this. Must visit just before sunset, so you have time to see the turtles and if your lucky -  you maybe able to witness the release of the little ones back to the sea.

Decent place to spend an hour as the guide/owner explained about various kinds of turtles and how they operate. They let us play around with turtles and the money we give them is used for sustainability of turtles.

A very enjoyable hour spent here learning about the hatch & release of turtles. Some larger turtles being cared for as they have injuries which mean they can't be released & also turtles which are being rehabilitated ready for release.

The turtle hatchery is very small but worth a visit. you are able to pick up some of the turtles which is nice! And all the money goes to releasing them back into the wild. The manager talks you through a lot of the turtles which is a nice touch.

Great place to visit. The owner was very informative, he gave us a tour of the hatchery and was very open about the past of the hatchery (destroyed by the 2004 Tsunami, along with many of his family members). Best time to visit is around 9am, as this is when you're most likely to be able to release the baby sea turtles! There was a big group of us travelling (15) so we rang ahead to let them know that we were coming, might be worth a quick call if you're in a big group! Overall a lovely visit, highlight of my stay in Hikkaduwa!

We enjoyed the visit to the hatchery. The owner was informative and went into great detail into how the place is run and the importance of conservation. We learnt a lot about the turtles in his care. He was quite strict about people not touching the turtles and stopped the more 'exuberant' tourist from touching them, which was good to see. You had the impression he genuinely cared for his longer term residents. We recommend a visit to the place.

Went here to show turtles to the kids. They really enjoyed the visit. The hatchery itself is a small place with a few large turtles and few tanks of smaller newborns (I believe to be later released). Not sure of the authenticity of all the claims, but if it helps save a few lives, then what the hell.

Today, me and my friend went to the turtle hatchery after reading many good reviews on TripAdvisor. When we arrived we paid the entrance fee of 500 rupies each. After the short explanation about the turtles we saw that a group of children were holding the baby turtles and throwing them back in the water without any care about the turtles. I can understand children don't know this, but even the staff totally didn't care and did nothing about it. This place should be a safe environment for the turtles, but they don't care about the animals and their wellbeing, they only care about their money. I asked the staff what they are doing and why they don't say anything about the way people "play" with the turtles, they didn't had any answer and they said tourists like this. They even keep some of the turtles as. touristic attraction, instead of leaving them in the sea. There whole story about taking care of the turtles is worth nothing, they treat the animals bad and do only things which the tourists like so that they get money. If you decide to go there, please don't touch any of them, they get scared and don't like it at all.

The turtle hatchery is very informative and run with great consideration to conservation. It is an important educative experience. The turtles are at different stages in their respective tanks in order to release them again. Some are injured through fishing.

This was a great little place , they seem to be passionate about saving/caring for the turtles there and we learnt a lot. We released 8 little turtles into the sea and was a very touching experience, our daughters loved it

One of the best turtle hatchery in sri lanka.  They teach about the Turtles in sri lanka and speciality of the each type. If you wanna touch or cuddle a baby turtle this is the best place to visit. Never miss this place if you travel Hikkaduwa. Trust me It's worth.

The staff here seemed very committed to the conservation and preservation of turtles and the man who showed us around gave a good explanation of the species and life cycle of turtles.  The messages about the effects of environmental pollution came through loud and clear.  Visitor facilities are fairly basic despite the large number of visitors.
This was interesting and a lot of fun. You can get all cuddly with the baby turtles and you are also allowed to hold the bigger turtles. Definitely great to do if you have children.

If you are in Hikkaduwa or passing through, you should stop by the turtle hatchery. It is a place where turtles are reared and taken care of. The turtles are in big tanks. The turtle hatchery we visited is a little north of the railway station. The walls outside are covered in colourful turtle themed pictures. As you enter the hatchery you can observe many large tanks for different species of turtles. There are sign boards giving plenty of information. There is a separate section inside the hatchery covered in sand where the turtle eggs are hatched. The kids were thrilled to release some hatchlings to the sea, which is done in the evenings. So the best time to visit the place is in the evening, closer to dusk.
Very cute turtles and nice to see them up close. Very impressed with their work with the injured turtles.

Generally the sanctuary appears to be managed by individuals who seem earnest in their concern about turtle conservation. However the kitsch tourist shop kind of spoiled it for me. However all said and done, for those who have never had the opportunity before, this visit may prove to be worthwhile. One point that stayed in my memory was seeing turtles taht were maimed by fishnets or by boats or turtles born with physical defects due to the effect of pollution of the sea. Although it was disheartening it was a stark reminder for all of us to bear about the importance of our responsibility towards keeping the environment we all live in healthy.
Amazing experience. The guy who looks after the turtles is so passionate about that he does and you even get to hold the turtles.
Lovely little place where my daughter enjoyed meeting the turtles. We had a lady who walked us through the various types. We got to hold the small ones and thoroughly enjoyed it.

I am sure this is a worthy cause but we did not feel comfortable about the way the turtles were treated.  They are taken out of the pools for the tourists to pose with, not what we wanted to be part of.  Our guide also asked us to compensate him for his time as our entrance fee was not used to pay the 'volunteers'.

This was an amazing experience as we where able to gently hold the baby turtles and our boys loved that, the staff where lovely and we where fortunate enough to release a baby turtle each to the ocean. The only thing was in my heart it felt wrong, the tanks where small and was unsure if those larger turtles where ever to be released. Also we where told people sell the eggs to the Hatchery that they dig up as otherwise they are often sold and eaten. If that is the case then at least many of the baby turtles are being set free. It was a beautiful experience setting them free especially having raw emotions from visiting a Tsunami museum only 20mins prior.

For just 500LKR per person, this is really not to be missed if you're staying in or around Hikkaduwa! It's great to learn about the conservation efforts of the hatchery and you get a good intro to all the different types of turtles there. You're even allowed to hold certain ones! We were lucky enough to visit on a day when we could release some of the babies (only a few days old) back into the sea! Such an amazing experience, and one which you won't forget in a hurry!

Very cute place with interesting trivia about turtles. Kinda makes me sad to see the disabled turtles, but I guess it's better than to leave them to die in the ocean. The small ones are adorable. Visit is very cheap and I recommend it to everyone in the area.

By visiting here you're also giving to a good cause, which is the conservation and hatching of turtles. We saw how the eggs were out in the sand, the small pools with turtle baby's and also the bigger ones which was regaining strength from injuries and such. Definetly worth a visit for anyone 👍👍

This was a nice visit to a small Hatchery. I think there were about 15 tanks with a variety of types of sea turtles. Some injured and recovering and others from babies to growing up. Good informations on types of turtles and best ways to interact with turtles. Also this place was big on conservation by educating the local populations. We paid 500rps for each adult and nothing for the child of 10. About 1 mile outside of hikaduwa.
This is a must see for everyone. The staff are very positive and informative. This place allows people to get really close and actually handle the turtles. A very positive experience and only 500 Rs.
Great short tour and hope their work helps to increase turtles in the ocean - they really need the help.  Keep up the great work!

This is a small turtle hatchery where the workers there save the turtles from other wild life on the beaches ect, look after them then set them free. It was a lovely experience for very cheap and it was just a nice experience to see people doing something for the animals in their community. They need donations to help them progress and keep helping the turtles.

good effort by the guy who runs the place.... it is a real heart warming experience to get up close with these awesome creatures but also heart breaking to see a few of the large turtles injured by fishing nets ...

I visited the sanctuary with my partner and her sister. We had no idea what to expect but were blown away with how friendly and interactive the staff were. We were given a 10-15 minute explanation of the different turtles and the danger they face. We were able to hold the turtles which I know can be controversial but also an amazing experience. We saw many amputated or partial rehabilitated turtles that would have no chance of survival in the wild. The highlight was releasing some baby turtles back into the ocean. The whole experience was truly genuine. The owners story is full of tragedy but overwhelming hope. I recommend all those that go to give generously and think deeply.
You can see just born turtles and some old turtles up, close & personal. Great place to learn a bit about turtles. Go in the morning to see the hatching.
It was just sad to see this caged turtels.. personal wasnt friendly... the price was to high.. i expectet complete different thing.. sorry but this was just bad

It's always so nice to see people  who genuinely care about animals & devote their lives to helping them.Well worth the visit & the entry fee should be more!!! It's clear to see this is not for profit and is purely to help turtles, especially injured ones. Everyone must visit when In Hikkaduwa!

The place which was established by a passionate man who faced a series of unfortunate events, is now run by his surviving family. They have a small entry fee which goes towards running the place. There is a guide who will take you through the small place explaining about the different types of turtles, their life cycles, how they are bred & rescued. One would also get to touch a few baby turtles which was a first for us. We spent 30 mins here & was totally worth it. Must visit!

Lovely man who owns and runs this turtle hatchery, doing amazing conservation work for these beautiful creatures, especially having had to rebuild the hatchery after the 2004 tsunami. We were also lucky enough to be invited back to help release a whole load of baby turtles back into the ocean one evening at sunset. An experience that both my husband and I, and especially our young children, will never forget!

So, it's a place where turtle's eggs are hatched and then post few days they r left in nearby sea. They will take you through the whole process of showing the egg, 1 day old turtle, 2 days old and 3 days old, post tht they leave them in sea. Apart from this they have different types of turtle (blind, genetic problem which makes them white, disabled turtles). They will let you touch 3 days old turtle and you can hold some bigger one on their permission. Nothing more to explore out here. Personally we just ticked mark this spot by visiting and got few pictures clicked but nothing which made us go wow!
Small Hatchery doing their bit to take care of the turtles. We got to hold the little turtles and the staff were very friendly and helpful.

We visited here a little unsure what to expect..... but loved it They hatchery rescues injured turtles and rehabilitates them to be able to be released again when they can be self sufficient. They hatch eggs and release them into the sea... quite a small place but interesting all the same

I went here to see some sea turtles and wasn't disapiointed at all. Very nice to see and even touch them. The people working there were very nice to ley tou hold the turtles and give a good explanation. Not so far from hikkaduwa (just take a tuktuk, not expensive at all to get there)

We found out that even though the hatchery has government accreditation, it is not a sanctuary but is a business.  What they are doing to protect the turtles is good but I feel that the ponds/tanks the turtles are kept in should be a lot larger to allow the turtles the freedom to swim more.

Was a wonderful experience. A turtle conservancy run by the world wild life federation where they take care of the worlds rarest species of turtles and also hatch new ones. For srilankan RS. 1500 per person you get to release 10 tuttles into the sea. Its an experience for sure!
Good initiative. Appreciate the work they are doing.  Nice interactive session. Kids will love the experience. Especially when you get to hold the young turtles.

We visited in April and found we were the only ones there due to it being the off season. It was great to walk around and get hands on the turtles. The sanctuary looked like a genuine conservation effort which was good to see and the guys working there knew their stuff. We were allowed to pick up and hold turtle of all shapes and sizes and get photos. They all looked in good health. At the end there was a chance to donate to the sanctuary.
We loved it. Saw lots of turtle babies and rescued turtles. They rescue the turtle eggs and hatch it on their own release them when they are ready.

Myself and my friends visited here on a weekday and it is located at a convinient place. Realy appriciate that their aim is to make a better and safer home for the turtles. Learnt a lot about turtles, good place for kids too.
Very good hatchery located on amazing beach. Kids will love to see turtles. Beach is good specially at Sunset time.
It's amazing to see baby turtles up close. The older turtles are beautiful all in their own way even when they are missing a limb.
The folks over there do a good job trying to maintain the balance of nature and help the turtles survive.

There are lots of turtle sanctuaries in Sri Lanka, but I didn't feel as though the owners of this one took us too has the best interests of the animals at heart. It was called 'Sea Turtle Hatchery E.K. Amarasena Fernendo' - down a little side street about 10mins from Hotel Riu. We were taken first to a sandpit where the turtle eggs hatch. The guide bent down to a pile of sand and dug around to find 3 baby turtles who had 'just hatched' - however, there were no egg shells which suggested that they'd hatched before we'd arrived and re-buried to give the impression that they'd just been born - unfortunately one of the three turtles had already died and was quickly hidden from our view. You're then taken to 'release' the hatched turtles into a tank which is almost filled to the brim with other baby turtles. You're encouraged to pick them up and play with them which is probably distressing for the little ones who are all trying to swim out and up the walls - some of these turtles had also died, and others just looked absolutely exhausted. After this, you can walk around the other tanks to look at the older, fully grown turtles that have been 'rescued' or who have been 'bred' at the sanctuary. These tanks are TINY. Hardly any room to swim, and the owners kept picking turtles and asking if you wanted to take a photo holding one. Although it's tempting to get a photo holding one for Facebook, oils/suncream/human bacteria on skin can be damaging for turtles, and it can be distressing for them to be constantly picked up, so please think about this if you are offered one to hold - it's nicer to just let them swim and be undisturbed... Finally, the last turtle you see is a big albino turtle. Again, this turtle is in a TINY tank which is hardly bigger than its body. It just stares into the corner and hardly moves - so sad. The whole 'experience' cost 500Rs per person, but another 'owner' then came up to us at the end and kept pointing at a donation tin to guilt-trip you into giving more money which I can’t see going towards the turtles care. It was just really sad. We went to a difference sanctuary later in the holiday (Arun&Aman Conservation Centre (with two big turtle statues over the entrance) and they seemed a lot more knowledgeable/caring, so it’s worth going to a more established one that you know is doing good. Just left this one feeling so sad for these beautiful creatures.
This is a serious sea turtle hatchery with no gift shops. The tour guide is a scientist working at the hatchery. We held turtles and were invited back to release baby turtles into the sea. Memorable!

We visited with young children and the owner did a good job of explaining which turtles he was fostering, patiently answering our kids questions, and making the visit nice. However the highlight was when we came back in the evening and released 50+ turtle babies into the sea... was an incredible experience for adults and children which we will always remember!

I can't be completely sure if turtles are treated well all the time, or if all the information given by hosts is true. But I am sure I had a good time visiting the place, having a chance to watch this creatures so closely and even touch them somehow makes you happier. Watching little ones being let go to the ocean is awesome. I really hope this sanctuary does much more good for turtles than harm them.

This place is run by the brothers of the original owner (who died in the Indian Ocean tsunami). Although turtles are protected by law, there's a great deal of poaching and illegal sale of turtle eggs. This hatchery protects turtles by providing a safe place for eggs to hatch, and by looking after injured adult turtles. All turtles are later released back into the sea. This is a great place to see and learn about sea turtles. You can touch/pick up the younger turtles (I really hope it doesn't scare them to be touched by humans). Entry fee of LKR 500 goes towards the upkeep of the place. These guys could do with more support. This place is located in Peraliya/Telwatta, right on the Colombo-Galle highway (A2), close to Hikkaduwa beach, and accessible by bus and tuk-tuks. There's a giant Buddha statue opposite the hatchery (that's your landmark).

On a recent holiday to Hikkaduwa I had the pleasure of visiting this gem! I got a tuctuc from my hotel to the hatchery where the driver kindly offered to wait and then bring me to the nearby tsunami museum (well worth a visit!). For 500 rupees you can explore the hatchery with its different species of turtle ranging from newborns to rescued animals. The owner gave us a tour and we were able to pick up the baby turtles which I particularly enjoyed! Well worth a visit!

From our hotel in Hikkaduwa we got tuctuc to the turtle hatchery followed by a trip to the tsunami museum close-by which I definitely would recommend. Baby turtles had been hatched in the morning we arrived. 500Rupees was an excellent price to enter, it is possible to hold some of the smaller turtles. Great experience.
500 rs to get in, definitely worth it! Turtles are well looked after and the guy running the place had alot of knowledge

There were many students having a day tour when we visited this place, they were friendly and nice but very load, I guess they were more exited than us visiting the sanctuary. Generally a nice place to visit.

With just a 500 roupies ( 3,5 dollars ) ticket ( whiich goes for helping the turtles ) you can see somekinds of seaturtles really close Learn some things for their lives and even touch them ( they really like it ) You will also see some handicap ones :(((

This place has a history going back to before the tsunami of 2004 when it was destroyed (and the owner lost her life). It is extremely well run by the same family who established the sanctuary and clearly provides an important service. They allow visitors to handle the young turtles and not everyone will agree with this approach but our 3 yr old was absolutely delighted/thrilled to be able to actually touch these beautiful creatures. He has pictures to remind him of this visit and I have no doubt that he will grow up respecting these animals and will want to help preserve their habitats, maybe because he was allowed to touch one when he was 3 years old.

This place educates you all about turtles. You get to watch turtles in all stages of growth, learn about their needs,hold them, watch them on land as well as on water. There are many species here, including albino turtles! This place is their sanctuary- one of the few in Asia.

I remember the board said A and Aman turtle hatchery. It was medium sized on the main road and behind was the sea shore. There were many varieties of turtle and of all ages. A local person explained very well in Englishand the turtles were really healthy. This was a complimentary visit from my tour agent and the driver said the tickets are srilankan Rs. 1000. Worth the money.

This place balances on the fine line between conservation project and money-maker for a local. While there is some useful information about turtles here, it is not anything that I remembered. The evening turtle release is supposed to be very enjoyable. It was interesting to see all the different types of turtles at various ages. For 500 rupees it is reasonable value but don't expect to stay longer than 30 minutes.

Oh I really liked this. It's not a big place but their work is important in keeping the turtles be a part of Hikkaduwa in the future and reminding everyone the importance of taking care of the enviroment. 500 rupies to enter and I gave some extra in donations. Wash your hands BEFORE and AFTER if you handle the turtles - be kind to both turtles and your self :-)

On our visit we didn't see the use of this place at all. When we arrived we were asked rudely to pay 500 rupees each and then allowed to go inside. All there is is around 15 ponds with turtles. In our eyes too little for most of them. After a while a guy from of the institution started explaining a little about the turtles but it seemed more like a "must-do" and he was not into it at all. When they even allowed tourists to hold up the turtles (pure stress for them!) we left the place super disappointed. This is just a tourist trap! The rescue of the turtles stands back.

The turtle Station cares on sick or damaged e.g Motor boats and learn them to survive. Also they buy turtle eggs and put this into warm Sand util baby turtles leaf the eggs and bring them to the ocean. The Staffel explained the different situation of each individual. A great experiance.

A smaller shelter with a variety of turtles from the green to the leatherbacks. The turtles on show are kept in small concrete pens which isn't great for the turtle but these are released at certain times so they eventually have freedom. There are many signs that give info about the turtles on show or the keeper will give information at request. A couple of the pens are open for touching and getting pictures, wish there was a bit more care taken from people holding the turtles or better information from the keeper on not holding them away from the water so if accidentally dropped they fall in the water and not on the floor... Only 500rupee per person so not expensive and quite educational. We were regularly approached to do this as a tour for 6000 rupee per person, do not do this as a tour!! ,This place is easily accessed by just renting a scooter  (which we did) and will save you a lot of money. Only about a 5 minute drive from hikkaduwa beach towards the police station.

It was interesting to see what is being done to protect the various turtles. Even the fisherman are aware of this and bring any injured turtle to the hatchery for treatment. The visit only takes 15 minutes but so worth it. Ask for someone there to advise you on what it is about.

Lovely little place to find out about these beautiful creatures, it was 500 SR to get in, about £3. Once inside there are many turtles to see and handle.It is a very small place so wont take long to look around, we had our tuk tuk driver wait for us. We were lucky enough to be able to release some baby turtles into the sea, which was one of the best things ever, my 11 year old son said it was the best moment of his life. We will definitely visit here again on our next trip to sri lanker

Great little place. Happy to pay the 500 entrance fee for the good work they do. All the different turtle species, lots of one day old turtles too. It was sad seeing the injured turtles though. We went back in the evening to see the babies go into the sea, it was amazing. My favourite part about my Sri Lanka trip!
This is only a small place but they are friendly and informative. It's certainly a worthwhile cause to support if you're passing

It was great to see the work put into conserving the turtles. We revisited in the evening to real ease the babies that had hatched that morning. A very special experience. If you have kids make sure you visit and ask about releasing.

We had such a great time at the hatchery. We arrived a day before he was releasing the baby turtles into the ocean so he allowed us to come back the following day free of charge to help release them. Would highly recommend for animal lovers!

This little place located 3km north from Hikkaduwa is supposed to be a rescue place for harmed turtles. When we arrived we got told straight away to pay 500rupees each in a harsh and unfriendly way. Afterwards we were allowed to walk in where we saw 15 small cement pools and a small sand area (for eggs apparently). There was a guy that told something about the turtles but he didn't seem into it at all. After his short talk he let the tourists pick the turtles up, also the big ones so they could take photos. It all seems like more of a money machine and a rip off than a rescue for the animals! Therefore we only give it one star and wouldn't recommend it.

The turtles are in small concrete tanks and have barely any room to swim. When asking the owner why the tanks were so small he said he was following regulations and the proceeded to tell us he was closing for the day even though it wasn't 6pm. I'm very upset that I have my 500 rupees to this man as I don't feel that he cares about the animals that he looks after.

Was nice to see the turtles so well cared for. They even let us hold them. Don't need to spend long here. They explain story of why they keep the turtles on the way round. Cost 500rp and all goes to care for the turtles

An interesting and worthwhile stop for 30 mins. As well as being instructional, it is also a conservation and rescue centre for these lovely creatures, many of whom have been injured by fishermans nets or boat propellers or other human activity.  See creatures from the agh stage to over 100 years old.

Traveled there with Lionel in the afternoon, there seemed to be no crowds at this time , Found it small,friendly,informative and great experience especially for  the other visiting family with young kids who very much enjoyed their visit ,Well worth it to include this on your itinerary .and would recommend looking out for Lionel (0777040088) at J.L.H Restaurant , Hikkaduwa who is very flexible as to what you want to do and when.

We visited the hatchery on our way from Ella to Hikkaduwa, it was a nice stop. We learned quite a few new facts about turtles and their life. Hatchery takes care of turtles' eggs, as well as of adult injured turtles and makes sure to release them all back to the sea once they are ready to swim. It was one educational visit.
Nice to see bigger and smaller turtles. Good to visit with kids and on days it is too hot for the beach or raining

Definitely worth a visit , especially good to see baby turtles being released to the sea😀. Friendly, informative staff and well worth the entry fee. Consider a donation too, to help with running costs.

Three sentences in Lonely planet guide on turtles in Sri Lanka were more informative than the "guide" at this hatchery. Basically they tell you to read the info boards, leave the money and go. Only after we've asked for some information, unwilling guy came, recited for 1min and closed with goodbye and thank you. The cause may be noble, but if they would be more informative about it, it would be easier to believe it.

I would recommend visiting this hatchery, it is family run and relies solely on donations as well as a small fee for entrance. The guy who runs it does an exceptional jib single handedly helping to preserve the turtles.
This was a great experience. It very nice to see people who care about animals and give them so much love. Very informative, learned a lot about turtles.
Great family project one should support! Many turtles are shown and explained. Even baby turtles can be seen :)
Should go here to see and if permitted hold a day old turt! 500 lkr is worth it to support the work they do!

If you have little time or you want little bit rest from sun you can visit this turtle farm. Entrance is 500LKR/ person. It's not big farm they have about 13 tanks full of turtles (big ones/medium/little ones). It takes you about 30 minutes.

They have few tanks with big and small turtles and they will give you nice guide who really says and explain interesting facts about turtles and their lives. They actually rescue the turtles hurt from the sea and help the turtle eggs to be born. If you are there give them also some donation is really worth it. If you are lucky they will show you how little turtles are born and will release them to the sea in the evening. The hatchery sign can be seen from the main road. Every tuk tuk driver knows this place and if you have your own car and cant find it on gps just go on the main street in directions to Colombo and find Tsunami memorial and the hatchery is just opposite the street. The hatchery is opened usually from 9am-6pm.

There was an entry fee of Rs 500 for adults, but free for kids. There are tanks with different kind of turtles - which are kept for educational purpose or for treatment in case they are injured. there is also a section where the eggs of the turtles are kept in sand and taken care of as they wait for the hatchlings to come out. The day we visited, some hatchlings of green turtles and olive riddley turtles had hatched the previous evening.they were supposed to be let into the sea the evening we visited. the owner /  manager gave us an informative tour telling us about the various turtles kept there. some turtles are allowed to be taken in our hand also. my daughter was very excited and happy.
This was a very nice short visit, looking about and we got to hold some of the baby turtles. And there's a box for donations.

500 rupee entrance fee to support the fantastic work they do here to support the various turtles that are challenged in this part of the world is such a small amount to pay. You can see all types of turtles and the guide really knew what he was doing! Although some people would say they are playing god to theses creatures you can't help but think they are due some help from humans considering what we do to harm them!!

The sanctuary is relatively small but the visit is very informative and wonderful for a family.  We managed to release some baby turtles into the ocean at sunset, so this was a very magical experience! The hatchery is a very worthwhile cause, so I would definitely recommend a visit.

We'd visited this place in a hurry because it got really late, and the owner was sweet enough to wait past their closing time of 6pm, till we got there. He was really nice and let us release the hatched baby turtles into the sea, which was a wonderful experience. We did see a couple of tanks with much larger turtles in them, some tanks seeming too small. This part we don't know about properly, because we went only to help release the baby turtles. Except for maybe the size of the tanks for the adults, this is a good place. Don't know if people are allowed to handle the big turtles, and I hope they aren't.

Place is quite small and it takes only a half an hour to take a tour, but it is worth to visit. You can actually held the baby turtles  in your hand. They were so cute. 1000 rupias per person with a private guide.
Not that big sanctuary, but the host buys off, keeps turtles and frees them. He continues his family "business". It worth to see. You can hold 2-weeks turtles in hands

This place has differnt types of turtles with differnt colors as well . Though the turtles are very small, you can still hold them in your hand they actually tend to show the whole life cycle of the Turtle . Interesting place.
Very nice experience, you can see many different turtles and even touch them. People there do a god job :)
please go and surport these people,they do great work,and good to learn more about the turtles,free to go in just leave a donation,please go!!!!!

We stopped here on a day trip from Negombo to Galle and saw the disabled turtles and the hatchery. While we were there baby turtles were being dug up and it was nice to see a baby just emerging from its shell. It was interesting to see two large turtles, one being friendly and the other known as Mr Nasty with a warning not to put fingers anywhere near it. At that point a young lady just had to do what she had just been told not to and the turtle gave a quite vicious snap of its jaws. Just a little closer and that would have inflicted quite serious harm. It is not a large place and there is little room between the tanks. It was good to see the breeding programme in force although I know that there is another school of thought that says it is better to allow nature to follow its own form of breeding.

Upon arrival we were told about the different types of turtles being hatched there. The guide then turned to a covered pile in the sand and dug up two premature baby turtles and planted one in my wife's hand before burying them again ready to be dug up again for the next guests. He showed us numerous tanks and showed no respect for the turtles, pulling them around for us to see and picking out the bigger babies for us to hold. Worst was the 'hospital tank', a small cramped tank with four large, diseased turtles. They would have been better off being set free to die in the ocean. The whole experience was unpleasant. We had hoped to avoid this kind of place but the tuk-tuk driver must have taken us to the wrong one. Be careful. If it looks cheap and shoddy, drive away and keep looking. There was a much nicer looking one a little further down the road.

This place is easy to get to in a Tuk tuk. It's 500 rupees per person and then you can look at the turtles in the tanks. It's a very small place and I was kind of disappointed. The adult turtles don't look well looked after and need bigger tanks. The owner gave us a little speech about the turtles but it wasn't all that interesting or informative. It's worth a trip, but it's not the best thing to do in Hikka.

It's an interesting place in Sri Lanka to see the turtles hatchery place which is near the beach, as you can see the real story how the turtles can put their eggs and the cycle of their life till go Back to the sea water , and you can see the different young age and different types of turtles especially those have genetic defects as blindness, no shells, no arms and also you can carry them and taking photos for memorial service

This is a small turtle hatchery. When I was there there was a school class there at the same time and then it got a bit noisy and crowded. But I had the chans to hold turtles that had just been hatched that day and that was awsome!
Nice job done by owner. Interresting to see. Thank you. Small but fine. Určite treba vidieť. Odporúčam.
Protecting  and caring for turtles; handicap-turtles, turtles of all age, even some just some hours old to feed until they can servive in the sea/the real world

Informative, interesting, a must do in Hikkaduwa and all for a great cause. Make sure you arrive or return for the 6pm turtle baby release. Fantastic moment where you help to release hatchlings to the sea!
We went in the day and learnt about the species of turtles and how the are threatened. It was lovely to come back in the evening and release babies into the sea a truly amazing experience

It's interesting to hear how they work with the turtles and from friends, who had visited the day before we had heard that it was excellent, however we experienced the staff as being uninterested in telling about their work other than the standard speech.

This is quite a small place and it is difficult to understand how much of an impact they can have but the value of educating tourists cannot be underestimated. I am fascinated by animals and love turtles so I enjoyed our visit. The tour was full of good information about the various species swimming in the 12 tanks. Just loved the hatchlings.

Again another good place if you are with children. I know there are mixed feelings about places like that but I personally think people who work there making more good than bad to the environment. We were allowed to take the turtles out of the water ( I am not sure if that is good but kids enjoyed it) and also we were so lucky to be invited for evening release young turtles to the sea. 500 LKR per person (kids free) I think is worth it.

This place was set up by the government to protect the 5 species of sea turtles in Sri Lanka. The money of paid for entrance was used to maintain the site. A guide would show you a sand place where there were various eggs at various stages. You could see baby turtles at day 1, 2 and 3. They were so cute! There were turtles with genetic defect which might not be able to make it to the sea, and those which were disabled by either shark attack or tsunami. There were two albino turtles. It would really be worthwhile to visit as you would be contributing to the survival of sea turtles. The site was simply set up, which would reflect how the money actually contribute to the turtle.

While in Sri Lanka we visited a few turtle hatchery's and sanctuary's and this is by far my favourite. It is only 500LKR which is the going rate but here we got taken around, not just left to ourselves. It was by a young girl, no older than around 12 and she knew everything! I was so impressed, she knew all the ages and breeds of turtles. Then for an extra 500LRK we were able to release some into the sea from a beautiful beach. We were able to choose which ones from eggs that we hatched the night before, so they were so small. It was an amazing experience to watch. Once the tour was finished her mom came out to ask how she did and we tipped them an extra 1000LKR and they were so grateful. They were then talking to us about our lives asking where we were from and offering suggestions on where to visit. Some how it came up in conversation that because we were tourists tuk tuk drivers were trying to charge us lots of money, so then she offered to drop us off in their own personal tuk tuk. Lovely family, lovely place. Definitely recommend a visit.

Visiting a turtle hatchery in Hikkaduwa is a must. It was such an interesting experience! The staff go to great lengths in their turtle conservation endeavors. You get to see the eggs buried in a little sand pit, to newly hatched babies - you even get to touch them in their tank - so cute! It's a sad and eye-opening experience seeing first-hand what damage humans are doing to sea life; yet heartwarming to see how much others truly care to help.
Very nice work with the turtles They care a lot about them protect them and everything there is very clean Nice to get closer  with these amazing creatures
Here you could see how the authorities are trying to protect the turtles from extinction. The white turtles was rear sight.
Very good explanation by the volunteers there regarding the turtles. You are able to touch and hold the turtles. Once in a lifetime experience. Will recommend this place.

I sincerely hope that most of the  Turtles are treated well and released after their rehabilitation . It seems that the pens are quite small for such lovely creatures. But a number have damaged flippers due to fishing nets ect so are not able to survive in the wild .  Most of the turtles are sponsored so I hope they will,make a success of releasing back to the wild

Worst place to visit the hatchery. You will see and learn how turtles give birth to various eggs but the staffs were not friendly. They allowed many chinese people to play with their turtles and all those tourists were happly taking out them from water just to take fotos. Then they were throwing them in water just like that. From kids to old age people, all were like that. No proper discipline was followed. Sad to see animals being treated like that. 1000LKR is the charges for one person which is not even worth. I will recommend, dont visit.

We all loved it. the guys who work there do care for this beautiful creatures very much. We visited another hatchery and they were very rough with the turtles. Go to this one and help them send more little ones into the sea.

On the road there are 4 or 5 of these places that want to show how they are taking care of sea turtles. This one costs 500 Rupees , others cost 1.000. A person of your language tours you around for 20 mins and tells you types, harvesting, rescue. You are allowed to touch many of them and even hold one on you hands. My guide showed me clips when baby turtles are released to ocean or when big mama comes up to deliver 100 eggs.
Great to see young turtles being saved but older turtles kept in concrete tanks for years

We visited here twice. Only Rs 500 entry for adults and you get to see a range of turtles and if you are lucky enough like we were you may get to see them being hatched!! Incredibly experience where we got to help hatch them and place them into the water tanks. At around 6pm some nights you can help put the 3 day old turtles into the sea which is very cool and amazing thing to do!!! The owner is very knowledgable and will answer all the questions you have! Highly recommend going!!

I think this place is well-run, and the kid who showed us around was knowledgeable, informative and able to answer questions well. If you take everything he says at face value, this is a great place that helps a lot of sea turtles. If you don't take everything at face value, it's a little disconcerting. They wait for a turtle to lay her eggs and then they dig them up and bring them here. They claim to be doing this to help the turtles survive - however, I'm pretty sure baby sea turtles need to walk down the beach after hatching to remember where to come back when they're adults. I asked about this, but they feel it's more important to release stronger sea turtles than to imprint them with the memory of a beach. I don't know about that - I'm not an expert. There weren't any babies there when we visited. However, if they are releasing the turtles back into the sea, then I'm happy for that. There were some injured turtles when we were there that they say they are nursing back to health. Again, if true, a worthy cause. Being a skeptic, I think there are some that are there permanently to have something to show visitors. Not much different from a zoo in that respect, but with the ocean just a few yards away, it seems sad. We did get to hold some turtles and my kids loved that. I think the kid who showed us around genuinely loves turtles and talking about them and he did a great job. I'm just not sure I believed everything he said.

This was one of our highlights in Sri Lanka. We had been sceptical about the turtle hatcheries, but this was fantastic. The owner was very knowledgeable and happy to explain everything there is to know about turtles. We got to the hatchery about 4pm and the owner offered for us to look around then come back to release the turtles at 6pm with no extra charge. We were extremely luckily as this doesn't happen every day. We got to see the baby turtles hatch and helped to dig them out of the sand and place them into the tank, and then later release them into the ocean. The whole experience was incredible and it is definitely for the good of the turtles, I would highly recommend you visit to experience these beautiful creatures up close.
À visit to the hatchery is a need to do and a nice to do thing when you visit Hikkaduwa. Your visit contributes to the survival of the turtles.

What this man does is just amazing. Little center but learned a lot and the owner is clearly passionated about his work. He does a great job educating people and helping the turtles futur. I absolutely loved it
contains horrifying but true picturs and photographs of the devastating tsunami including snaps of rrelief-rehabilitation work carried out.
If you're already in hikkuduwa or on the way to Galle Fort, might as well drop by on the way to see the turtles, nothing too special. I spent around 10 mins there, entrance fee is 1000rs per person

We had a Great time visiting the turtle hatchery..amazing work being done to help endangered species. Being able to see (and hold..) some of these beautiful animals was a joy.. We were lucky enough to help release a few back into the wild which was an experience we will never forget Keep up the great work Butler family uk

The owner explained the idea of the place really good, we had a good experience! At the beginning I was a little concerned if the place was good for the turtles but as we got more knowledge places like this are important to maintain number of turtles in the sea! Good place for kids!

This is a superb place to visit - a couple of folks who rescue turtles and nurse them to health, as well as provide hatchlings a place to grow before being put back into the ocean. The chaps there will gladly take you on a tour of the place. The Rs 500 entry fee is more than worth it, and you can make an added contribution at the end. You can play with some of the turtles and it's a super experience :D Those complaining that it's 'boring' are missing the point of the place - it's not a place to just ogle at turtles but also understand what they're doing. If just animals is what you want to see, try a zoo. This is a sanctuary to rescue, protect and nurse turtles. PS: GoPros are the best to record under the water ;)

Sorry but this is no visit worth. Maybe if you never have seen a turtle you can go there just because it is cheap. Otherwise there is nothing interesting. I did not get any explanation and in 2 minuit you can finish it because it is really tiny and nothing happens.
Knowledgable owner who rescues injured turtles and nurses them back to health. Great to see baby turtles!!
This is a great hatchery, rescue turtles and baby turtles to hold and learn about. Pleased to see an attempt made to keep the turtles safe and thriving. Very informative tour

Its worth visiting if you have kids with you. The owner gives us the full information about the type of turtles and their features. They also allow us the handle the turtles which my son enjoyed. There was turtle whose 1 arm was hurt and weighed 40 kgs.. My husband picked that up and had amazing feeling.. Its worth a visit.

Definitely worth visiting. There were many turtles of all different breeds, along with many baby turtles (some only 3 days old) which we could hold which was a big highlight. There were also some turtles who had been rescued from losing a foot. The owner showed us around and explained about all the different types of turtles, showed us turtle eggs and his sandpit full of different turtle eggs waiting to hatch. He was very knowledgable and asked any questions we had. Some days he will release turtles into the wild so would be worth timing this if it permits, however we couldn't and still found this a very enjoyable experience. Nice to see the owner genuinely cares so much for these turtles and their environment.

I first visited this place in 2001 of course it was completely destroyed in the tsunami so its good to see that they have rebuilt it. They take and buy eggs that people would usually eat and rebury them until they hatch then keep the babies for a month or so before releasing them. This gives the baby turtles a better chance of surviving to adulthood. I admire them for doing all they can to save these highly endangered beautiful creatures. Please support by visiting and make an extra donation if you can to support their VITAL work. I asked the owner do you have a gift shop and he said no, I don't want people to think this is a business, we are here just to save the turtles! What a great man!

Our tuc tuc driver took us here and we were not disappointed very interesting and cheap to visit our guide was very informative and we found it very interesting my daughter loved holding the baby turtles

It's a must visit as you can handle the little turtles and they are so so cute Super worthy cause Owner is a pleasure too meet and you can sense the passion and indeed the great loss the Sri Lankan people suffered in the tsunami

I firstly understand that money is limited...however the 'tanks' in which these turtles are kept is unacceptable. Some of the older, larger turtles can barely turn around. They are simply square concrete pools with a little sand in the bottom. And to make it worse, some of the turtles have been living in these 'squares' for nearly 2 years just so that the visitors can look at them!! I was informed that they will be returned to the ocean eventually...but even so, 2 years is far too long to live in those conditions. In one of these squares, lives all the baby turtles that have newly hatched ranging from newly hatched to maybe 1 -2 months old. Visitors are allowed to handle the babies and whilst I was there, an ignorant woman picked one of the babies up very high from the water and let it fall from her hands as it tried to escape which ended in her laughing!! I immediately gave her in trouble for being so stupid and told her to kneel down and put her hands in the water and let them swim to you instead of picking them up. I informed the manager who also spoke with her but there is no supervision from the staff so I suppose this happens regularly... The manager seems to be doing his best but with the amount of visitors entrance fees they get I am sure they are capable of providing them with adequate space and tank enrichment.
Guide introduces you to the turtles! Then explains the work that they do and the different types of Turtles. They also have a turtle hospital Good value!

Visited the Hatchery, it is a small facility but well maintained, there are various types of turtles with information about hem displayed on boards. There is a lot of environmental awareness that is being created specially focussing on  human activities impacting turtles.  Must visit for all ages.

Plenty of baby turtles to see and hold. Few larger ones and a small speech from the boss. Highlight was seeing baby turtles released in the evening. Cost 500 rupees per adult and kids half price to go into tank area and nothing to see turtles released. Not something you would do every day and kids loved it so worth the small fee I would say. Turtles not release every day, so worth checking.
Me and my wife visited this place in 2014 . Was heartening to see people are looking after these creatures in danger. I would recommend a visit and give some sort of donation for this worthy cause
Not worth the amount you pay! You hardly see 5-6 turtles and how they are kept. Bad water and low hygiene. Give it a pass folks!
This is a small hatchery but worth a visit in addition to another attraction in the are. Some informative talks by the owner but it doesn't take much more than 30 mins in total
There is not much to this place but it is worth a visit if you like turtles. There is a short presentation and some time to walk around and see the turtles. Great for kids!

A good trip to see the turtles,  when you arrive you get a guide to explain the farm this is in the entrance price the baby ones are cute then you can hold the ones around 6 months and these are heavy.
Good experience and information on the turtles. It was however difficult to judge whether the turtles Kept in captivity was in 'good condition' - the tanks seemed very small

The hatchery is just a short tuktuk drive outside of hikkaduwa. It costs 500 rupies to enter and there is an additional donation box. The money is used for keeping the hatchery going. I understand the hatchery is there to educate people about turtles and therefore it's for a good cause. The owner also explained a few interesting things about turtles in general. And he explained that the turtles are to be released back into the ocean. However we found it sad to watch the turtles in the small tanks. Some of them are hurt and have no legs and arms. You are not allowed to touch them.
Simple but informative hatchery.  Manager takes time to explain rescue efforts and does a good job.  Ask your tuk-tuk driver to wait as it only takes 20 minutes or so.

This is worth a visit if you are staying in Hikkaduwa. You probably need only about 45 mins to look around this simple but informative hatchery. There is plenty of opportunity to see turtles of all ages and sizes up close. The manager is on hand to give information about the centre and the turtles.

The sea turtle hatchery is worth a quick visit with kids. The manager is very friendly and explains well to the kids. He's really kind and let the kids hold the baby turtles. Good for a afternoon visit and only 10 minutes in tuk tuk from Hikkaduwa village
enjoyed by my kids , a must see for all and a learning experience for kids and adults u must go there once

I was skeptical about the turtle place fearing that it would be displaying turtles for tourism purposes.  I was pleased to find that the turtle conservation is their main aim. They buy the turtle eggs from fisherman on the beaches out front and bury them in the sand in a protected area to hatch them and return them to the ocean.  Great 20 minute visit for the kids to get to learn about turtles and the challenges they face now.  You can feel good contributing the 500 rupee entry fee to this cause and hope that their efforts pay off in helping to save the turtles of Sri Lanka.

A nice place and they are doing some great work for the turtles. Entry is 500 rupees which is reasonable. They have around 14 tanks with different turtles in each. You can pick up the baby turtles. They lost a star as the owner started giving us information about the turtles for about 3 minutes and then looked at his phone and went away! He only covered 4 of the tanks. It would of been great if he had gone through each tank and told us more.

The people there are friendly and let you take the tiny turtles in your hand. The different types were shown to us and the owner describes nicely. The grave yard and the disabled turtles were sad to see . We liked it.

I read all the reviews before going and my family want to go because the kids want to see Tuttle's. So you can see and touch the little Tuttle's. The place is very small and looks old not like modern like you would expect. The guy came after 15 minutes for a small talk , where he keeps telling he needed money. He didn't get my questions about why they don't try to educate the people about Tuttle's. They buy the egg's because otherwise people will buy and eat them. Found it a little weird story with no backup behind it. It's oke for kids to see Tuttle's but the place feels not oke
I loved This place so Much!! Many different kinds of turtles, and even new born baby turtles. Really great man who runs the place with passion and not profit. Must go to place in hikkaduwa

Myself and my boyfriend are marine biologists so this was a must do while we were in Sri Lanka and we appauled everything they are doing here. The sanctuary is very small but they are doing the best they can with the facilities and knowledge they have. A number of turtles there are suffering from turtle buoyancy syndrome so it would be great if someone with the veterinary knowledge could help them deal with this problem and that way the turtle can be rehabilitated faster and returned to the ocean. You guy are doing a great job and I'm amazed at your resilience, particularly after your own personal tragedy from the tsunami and rebuilding the sanctuary. Thank you for inviting us back for the release and keep doing what you are doing!
This is a Great cause and helpful owner. Cutest little turtle buddies ever and you're allowed to pick up the babies. I think was well worth stopping in.
Interesting place with different stories of turtles, but be careful when you come also you could see handicapped turtles it's so pity.
Its a great initiative that we were happy to support by stopping by. Playing with the turtles was fun too.
Its a place where you can actually learn about the different speaces of turtles, the ticket you pay helps to keep going with their tasks...its a must in Hikkaduwa. Jose bcn
inexpensive and enjoyable. all for a very good cause. you can pick up the turtles while you are there, but i am not sure how much they like it. bloke that runs it is very nice.
Not worth 500 rs. I definitely expected a bigger place with more turtles for this price. They have approximately 10 backets with different turtles (small and big ones) and a small turtle cementary.

The guys at the turtle farm are doing amazing things to help and raise turtles. They have a good few on offer and work as a non profits organisation. I did the whole visit in 10 minutes. So I wouldn't travel out of your way to this place.
Organized , clean, staff great. Turtles cute. Kids loved it. We spent 1 hour there . Donation only required.

This place was on route to our visit down south to Galle, it was a last minute unexpected visit and I'm glad we stopped. It has lovely turtles of different type and the smaller ones you can actually pick up! Overall definately recommend as a stopover.

The hatchery is serving a super valuable purpose, full credit to them. Unfortunately they encourage the visitors to pick up and play with the baby turtles which can't do good things. Love their work, just not their tour.

Amazing experience where you are able to observe sea turtles that have been rescued for various reasons. They are well taken care of and along with an explanation of how the organization is run you also get to (gently!) touch the baby sea turtles and watch them playfully swim around. Very fun time and highly recommended!
Great experience getting to see the different stages of development of turtles, loved that it was promoted from a community level and was sustainable resource!

Good setup and nice that you can be quite handson with a lot of the smaller turtles. We got some great pictures and it's nice to hear that it's not just a zoo with the majority being put back into the wild as soon as possible.
it is nice to see that the local people are taking care of the nature in this country. several helpless turtles are saved here they staying and learning how to survive with there handicap over here

My friend and I visited here a few weeks ago, and it was absolutely lovely! It was so wonderful seeing all the turtles, little and large! It was so nice to see the turtles all being looked after so well, especially the ones that had received life changing injuries in their lives or born without limbs and would have otherwise died in the wild. The owner was so kind and spoke to us about the turtles and the hatchery. Would definitely recommend, we ended up staying here for some time learning about them all :)
Amazing.. Heartwarming... without these guys the turtles would be in decline... 🐢 Please give generously with your donation when there... they need our help bless them..

Went there today and had a great time. We got to release 10 baby turtles into the sea. The owner explained a lot about the turtles and his family. Please do not take a tuktuk straight to the hatchery. The owner has to pay 300rp of the 500rp entrance price to the driver. He uses the money of the donations and ticket prices to sustain the facility. Thank you for this amazing experience!

Situated around 4km from the Hikkaduwa beach you could either walk it down to this place or take bus. The money you would spend on a tuk tuk could be saved and donated at this hatchery. I was lucky enough to get a chance to release the turtles at this place which is usually in the evenings. It's a small place, however, the owner does what he can to safeguard the various species!

If you just want to see/hold a baby turtle this is a great place. The owners are doing a great job saving the eggs and babies but there is not much here. 12 or so small concrete tanks with different sized turtles. The owners whole family died in the tsunami and it's amazing to see him continuing his dads passion looking after the center. Wirth the 1000 for 2 people.

This Turtle hatchery is exceptional -  they let you hold every kind of turtle and take selfies or click you with these cuties. Be careful of the biggies - they can easily bite your hand off. The adjoining beach is pretty and you can follow the turtles' trail there to see how they come inland to lay eggs! Lovely experience!
This was an excellent and memorable bit of our trip. You get to handle the baby turtles. Lovely host, explained everything. Within walking distance of tsunami museum.

Great little find and really interesting to hear about how turtles were looked after and how the environment in the modern day are impacting their lives. Definitely worth visiting even if it is just to see little baby turtles .

To get there  just ask any tuk-tuk driver to take you. Once there the owner tells about the different  turtles and how they help them.  When we were there there were not a lot of newly hatched turtles since they had just released  them into the ocean. Worth a  short visit for maximum an hour.

We visited in October. The guy in charge over there was very nice and the place was clean and orgenized, he explained about the turtles and answered all the questiond we had, But that is not the main cause to visit. This guy is helping turtles, he helps injured ones live, those who had no chance surviving on theyre own. :)

We went to the turtle hatchery when staying in hikkaduwa. It was small but the tour guide for very informative and it didn't need to be any bigger. We got to hold the turtle and also shown how to tickle them which was really cute. Only 500 rps to enter and worth it

despite being quiet small, you get your moneys worth. The tour guide really invests so much time and effort in ensuring the turtles in his care are looked after. Recommend to anyone who is visiting Hikkaduwa or surrounding towns.

Nice place to visit and good to see organisations doing something to improve turtle life in Sri Lanka. Had a very informative guide explaining the process and how they return the turtles to the ocean. Well worth the visit
The place is small but very well maintained. The man who showed us around was very polite and friendly. Entrance fee was decent (500 Rs) and worth the stop.

We visited the hatchery during our vacation in hikkaduwa. We stayed there one and a half hour and it was really nice. We learned much about the different kind of turtles and hatching them up. We can recommend this place :-)

Short Tuk Tuk ride north of town to the hatchery. 500 rupes entrance fee and a short guided tour and explanation of their work. Able to pick up the very small turtles and view all of the others including the injured ones that are rehabilitated prior to release.

We went to a turtle hatchery but I am uncertain if this was the same one, as there are several along the highway.  Regardless, it was nice to see them caring for the maimed and homeless turtles and watching out for the young.
This is a nice little place. You can see rescued turtles and baby turtles. You wont spend much time there. Only 40 minutes or so. Entracne is free- just a small donation. I can reccomend it.

it was very well maintained. We were taken around and explained about all the different types of turtles there, the perils faced by them and the highlight was we were allowed to scoop up gently in our hands baby turtles , a big hit with our kids

Small place with separate small water pens for different aged turtles. Clean and the place looks well maintained. The high point is holding the turtles in hand and petting them. With a visit especially if you like animals

When we read about this Turtle farm we knew not to expect too much but still had high hopes to contribute something good for this amazing animals and also learn about the problems and challenges that this animals have these days. But NO. You'll get almost no information about turtles, the living conditions are horrable, and you really get the feeling that this poor guy who owns the farm hustle for his everyday living just like anybody alse on Sri Lanka- with getting some of this turist money. So if you want to learn about animals I suggest you go on Wikipedia and read about them, if you want to see them then go and rent a snorkeling equipment (plenty of of places around Hikkaduwa to see them in their natural habitat) and if you want to help turtles find a bit more efficiant organizations and donate to it!

The story behind the hatchery is very sad and the man that runs it does a wonderful job of rescuing the turtles that  otherwise may not have survived.  Would recommend for those wanting to learn about how pollution affects turtles and the effect the tsunami had on Hikkaduwa.

A great little place with heaps of info about the different turtles, their food pref's and expected life spans etc.. Rs500 entry which was well worth it, you can donate too which is good :) Loved seeing the turtle and learning about the rehabilitation for the older wounded ones.

We visited this hattery during our stay in Galle. A very well run establishment that we could see. Well worth the 500 rupee entrance fee. We were given a quick run down of the centre work and we're able to pick up specific size turtles. Thank you Keep up the fantastic work.

Visited as part of a tour package. Didnt expect much initially. However, it was such a worthwhile experience. The staff there are very knowledgeable and obviously passionate about stopping the killing of turtles. They do a variety of things for the turtles there, for example releasing the newborn turtles (which you can do at evening times) and looking after disabled turtles. worth a visit! you even get to hold the baby turtles, so cute..

It was raining a bit during our stay in Hikkaduwa so we wanted to drive around town. Came by this hatchery and we are happy that we went in. The owner really knows a lot about turtles and you can see that he does it with his heart. Even though the hatchery was completely ruined by the tsunami and even though he also lost relatives during this same disaster, he still continues this important work. The visit is worth the 500 rps if you know what the hatchery does with it. You'll see that you even want to make a donation. Go in and see what they do with your money, get educated and enjoy! Greetings from Holland!

... you must visit a turtle hatchery. I'm not sure what the other hatcheries look like but this one was pretty small. Nevertheless we had a fun time observing the sea turtles of different sizes, and we were even allowed to hold the smaller ones. I'm not sure if the story told by the owner is true but I give him the benefit of the doubt. Hopefully our fee paid (500 rupees) does contribute towards a better cause. It's Although I didn't get a chance to do it myself, this visit is best done in the evening when they release the turtles back to the sea (please check in advance as I hear it's not done Everyday).

Great conservatory effort to save turtles. The tour is guided by knowledgable and nice guide. They have a tiny ones (1-3 days old and super cute) as well as older ones. They also take care of disabled or injured ones. Th There is a big sandy area where the eggs are placed and then small turtles hatch. If you in season you can join the team to patrol the beach in search of eggs. The entrance fee is Rs500,

To me it really depends on your preference, I personally don't like seeing large animals struggling to swim around tiny little pools. The hatchery's are billed as a sanctuary to help breed turtles and look after them, however to me that didn't come across. It felt very much like a tourist attraction and a ploy to get money. I personally would not recommend.

If you an animal friend you will enjoy visiting this farm , you can see big and really small tartles and get an explanations about helping the tartles , there is a fee for getting in but it is a donation for keeping the farm working

Good collection of tortoise.  This centre take good care of turtles . There are handicapped turtles  ( like blind,  without limbs etc) also.  We also saw white (albino) turtle.  It's a place for must visit.  Entrance fee is only 5  dollars per person
Fascinating to learn about the turtles here.  Good to know some people are attempting to protect these sea creatures, and educate the rest of us.

Well informed guide who was a volunteer, allowed to hold a day old turtle I personally did not feel this was necessary. The turtles would hopefully be released into the ocean in time. The turtles who remain at the sanctuary and cannot be released for various reasons should have better tanks, perhaps if visitors gave more generously this could be achieved.

As others have said, the ticket is 500 LKR per person. We were a family with 5 adults and 2 children, and only paid for the adults. The whole thing took us about 30-45 minutes, with 15 minutes being an explanation by the owner about how they recieve the turtles and eggs, how they bury the eggs and wait for them to hatch, and then an explanation of the different kinds of turtles they have in the tanks. They had baby green turtles that we could hold. I'm not sure if this is good for the turtles, but I'm also a believer in the survival of the fittest, so I hope this somehow helps them when they get released into the sea. They had baby turtles, toddler turtles and a few other smallish ones, as well as big ones which were injured. It is a bit heart-breaking, so be warned if you're an empath.
We were taken by our tuk tuk driver as a stop off so had no idea what to expect, huge turtles in tiny little tanks made me want to cry I wouldn't recommend at all

Run by 2 brothers who lost their families in the 2004 tsunami. They explain the process of hatching the eggs and releasing the turtles. They also look after injured turtles. Entrance fee is 500 rs - very reasonable for the experience you get. We got to hold baby turtles which was defiantly a highlight. Would recommend.
It's very good place in hikkaduwa lot of turtles in there but not albino ones in there... When you go evening you release baby turtles....
worth for money. we get lot of information about turtles. The owner doing a valuable work. They rescue the turtles. It's was a good place for us.
We worth a visit the guy there was very informative and their work is in valuable to the turtle, they rescue the injured and if they are not able to return into the wild they loo after them.

I like what they are doing: rehabilitating turtles. I do not like that everyone can just grab the baby turtles and are encouraged to do so. In addition, the larger turtles are in small pools with little room to swim. I understand that they were saved and are being helped to survive in the wild again, but I would prefer if it was more "look, but don't touch"
