This was a great turtle conservation place. It was heavily damaged in the tsunami in 2004 but has recovered well. Turtles well looked after and released every day at 6pm. You can volunteer to help too
Its an very good thing if You Go there And Watch How The injury turtles get some help. Please give also Tips that The Projekt can Continue And grow
Popped  in following a trip to tsunami museum. Great little place doing a good job at educating tourists about the plight of the turtles around the world. Keep up the good work.

Not a great experience, but the do staff seem to be trying to do a good job with the little funding they have, Large Turtles are in kept in small tanks, and to western standards this appears cruel. Having said that if what the guides say is right most of the turtles there would not have survived in the sea as lots are brought in by fishermen now if they find them injured or trapped in fishing nets, where before the centre raised awareness they would have been killed. Visit to help the funding but be prepared for what you will see as some people will find this distressing
Great place Another great tourist attraction for hikkaduwa its small place but you can see many Turtles in there
It was amazing learning about turtles and also able to take photos with them. Good work is done by the owner  and also help us know the impact of plastic bags on the animals .

Turtle hatchery is quite ok for the price and not at all value for money...should go only if you are interested for learning about the turtles and entry ticket is kind of donation for the good activity done by the owner...
popped in on the turtles to have a look then my mother released some hatchling turtles back into the seaq

this was next to where we stayed so we thought we'd take a look, nothing fancy just a small place with multiple tanks, the man their explained about every type of turte, it was nice to know about them, this man lost his family in tsunami and now he is running the place in their memory, the ticket entrance is 500 rps/ person and it all goes to take care of this place. if you are around this area, take a look..

Went here as my partner wanted to see what it was about but I unfortunately found it quite depressing. I'd like to caveat this by saying I am a very firm believer than animals are mostly best in the wild and sometimes whilst humans are trying to help, we often aren't by intervening. The tanks are very clean and I genuinely believe that these people think they are helping, but I'm just not sure it's the right thing. One of my main issues here was that you're allowed to pick up the baby turtles (and encouraged to do so). I personally don't think a true conversation centre should allow people to touch the animals. They are already out of their natural habitat. Also, this place is branded as a hatchery but there are a lot of big turtles in small tanks. The owner assured us that the healthy ones are only brought there for a while to educate children before being released. Again, I found this sad because of the size of the tanks and also there wasn't much information on how successful this was. Most of the turtles seems to be swimming against the walls or not moving at all. Some of the turtles have been in accidents and they can't be returned to the wild because they wouldn't be able to swim properly. While I understand this, I can't imagine being confined to such small spaces would be beneficial for them considering how long they live. The owner explained that they buy the eggs from the market and hatch them and release the turtles back into the once just after they are born. I unfortunately read a few things online that explained how difficult it is for this process to be recreated and often the baby turtles end up with diseases. There are also now a lot of these places along the main Galle Road and little research to show that this type of place has helped with the declining number of turtles. Fine to visit if you like turtles and want to help aid their cause, but personally I think more education on the importance of these animals to people, rather than trying to recreate a habitat.

The tour guides were very friendly and knowledgable about the different types of turtles. They informed us that Nov-may is the best time to see the variety of baby turtles. It was a very nice experience.

Did a few days volunteer work here. It's pretty cool. It's houses around 10 larger turtles ranging from logger hears to leatherbacks and also baby turtles too. It is very much a tourist haven as they don't  really have the intention of releasing any turtles as it gets them their business.. (Hatcherys hatch eggs and release?) this is a downside to this place. The woman that runs it is demanding and quite rude but she does have a project to run so it's understandable. The tanks are small and the turtles look lost. If you why affected by wildlife being kept in confined spaces (small tanks for large turtles) it's not ideal. We helped clean a big tank that the charity I was volunteering for donated. Took a lot of work and pretty tiring. Positive to this is we got to hold a lot of the turtles and baby ones too. Worth a visit if you can look passed the small tanks. It's not a wasted trip!

For me, it was one of the higlights on our trip. Although i love turtles, they impresed me even more. Entrance is not expensive and i know it's going for the right purpose! The story behind family is sad, so I am happy they kept going. Turtles are all cute and interesting. I recommend! :)
You can see different types of turtles here.  They release the turtles after growing them unless they have a disability.

This place is really nice, they have all type of turtles that grow in Sri Lanka. It's a great thing what they're doing saving the injured and partless ones. I had a good time and paid a fair price for it.
Good to know about turtles ... Especially good if you have kids. Good explanation about turtle conservation and life cycle.
very good place to see baby turtles, and they give you some information about them, friendly people, very close to Hikkaduwa

Small place with about 14 tanks. The owner takes care of wounded turtles as well as hatching eggs. However, alittle bit sceptical about the place because the tanks were small, and place small in general and the public were allowed to handle the small turtles, dont know whether that is a good thing for the turtles, ok for the public, but is it ok for the turtles? He seems to know his stuff, but is it just for money?
The place privately run by Mr. B.K. Nimal and being run with donations. The hatchery and sanctuary takes care of the wounded and sick turtles.

Worth a visit, gf was slightly sceptical of while thing before going, but owner sounds as if he does a lot of education talks with local children and informs them of issues with fishing and reading eggs etc which went some way to alleviating or concerns. Good talk about the process and chance to see injured turtles and new born almost ready to be released. Philosophy was that turtles ideally do not want to be in ' prison ' like tanks so release as soon as possible.

Our guide took us here on the qay from.colombo to galle. The man that runs it gave us a quick run down on what he is looking to achieve and the varying species of turtle he has. He appears to have a real passion for his cause and i suppose and time will tell how he fairs. Definetely worth a visit on your way through.

Second time visiting the turtle hatchery. The first time we paid the entry fee (cheap) and then the owner gave us information about the turtles. He then asked us for tips at the end after giving us a spiel about how he lost his whole family in the horrific tsunami disaster. We obviously gave tips at the end. When I visited this year our driver (a really friendly local guy), who knew the owner of the hatchery well, laughed when I told him that story. He said it was lies! Anyway, whether the story is true or not, the hatchery is fine for the baby and smaller turtles but some of the larger ones are left to stagnate in small pools in the Sri Lanka heat. The story given is that they are injured and unable to return to the ocean (which may be true) but the pools are tiny and completely inadequate for these huge turtles

Being here is just so over-whelming, seeing the owner stand there so strong after everything he has been through and care for the turtles in the hatchery is just amazing. The story behind the hatchery is very touching and would 100% recommend this if you are in Hikkaduwa. The turtles are unbelievably cute (especially the babies)

Great work is being done by the owner of this place and his family. They rescue turtles and treat them and ensure they can go back safely to the sea. For injured turtles, they teach them to swim with the remaining limbs. Such great work! A must visit to this place.
Nice to see and learn about the different turtles. Small place but interesting worth a visit. I would think smaller children would love it.

Took a Tuk Tuk up here one morning. It is such a lovely little place! Lots of different breeds of turtle, varying sizes. The man is very knowledgeable. Can even hold some of the smaller ones. Not a big place, or somewhere to spend all day, we were there an hour or so, but definitely worth a visit.

Very interesting and a worthwhile cause. Good English speaking guide. Lovely to see the baby turtles hatched and ready to go back into the sea. It is a shame the tanks aren't bigger for the larger turtles though. It did make me feel sad for the ones that don't get to go back for whatever reason - I'm not sure that life in a 6 foot square tank is a great alternative....

We went here instead of going to the ones recommended by the tour rep. The guy who owns it explains how he buys the eggs stolen by the poachers to save the turtles. He also has turtles that have been injured in fishing nets. It's a great cause and a very informative hour. We all enjoyed it, and wish him all the best for the future of his good work

I am unsure if u visited this Hatchery or some place else but let me warn the all who come here sorry I am being specific as they think they have te right to dirty the water tank. Kids throw tissues in the tank it's their home. Don't do it. The tanks also take care of handicap turtles and hatch the new hatchlings. Take care

This hatchery is definitely worth a visit, the man who runs it explained everything perfectly and we saw every stage from eggs buried beneath the sand waiting to hatch to disabled turtles that he takes care of. We all thoroughly enjoyed a couple of hours here.

We went hear this morning. The guy there have us a talk all about the turtles. We were even able to hold them. It cost 500r to get in and then you could leave a donation which we did. Fantastic morning! Thanks

After reading some reviews we decide to visit this hatchery. We expected it to be a bit bigger not just 12 basins. Nevertheless the visit was nice. There are various species of turtles in preparation for their back to the wild. The owner of the hatchery gives description on each of the types of turtle and the problems they face in the wild. You receive also information regarding the turtle birth. You are also able to pick up the turtles.

I loved this place. Paid LKR 500 to enter hatchery (price for Foreigners) Not a large place, nor modern, but hey this is Hikkaduwa Sri Lanka and they are doing there best after losing so much in the Tsuanami. Owner was there and gave a great informative talk. Kept it simple which didn't make it so boring. Nice to see what they were doing for all the turtles that had lost limbs etc. Big plus was getting to hold turtles.

My kids had a great time and loved the visit. Staff were very friendly and informative. The place is small but packed with different types of turtles found in Sri Lanka.  My youngest son is turtle mad and is now a very happy camper!
Nothing much to miss. May be just a visit enroute should be fine. There is a old city place. Must go.

Small privately owned turtle hatchery ... Nice to see the babies and those being cared for after injury .... Worth a visit to get close to the turtles and understand the conservation work being done there

Myself and my partner visited the sanctuary during our stay in Hikkaduwa. We paid a small entrance fee and was then handed over to an English gap year student who was working at the centre. She was extremely knowledgeable about the turtles and the work the sanctuary does and answered all questions asked of her. Though the centre is small you get to see a number of different breeds of turtles as well as get to hold and have photos taken with certain breeds. The sanctuary does some remarkable work saving eggs, looking after injured turtles and releasing back to the wild. Though obviously desperate for funding we were not pressured for additional cash and the place is a must see.
Interesting in order to see how they try to safe turtle. Some of the are in the aquarium and You can take beautiful fotos Normally you cannot touch...
Not a large sanctuary, but nice friendly staff. Well worth a visit. The kids were able to hold a few of the baby turtles so they were very happy we visited!

Our guide was one of the many volunteers at the hatchery, and gave us lots of information. Even though she said that they don't want people to touch the turtles, another volunteer showed us how to handle them. We even tickled a turtle! There were also turtles who have eaten plastic, and are unable to dive under water so now remain at the hatchery. This turtle had a lot of fuss from my husband, and she loved it! It was a lovely visit, and even though it is small the hatchery do release turtles back into the wild and not keep them as a money making scheme. The owner lost a majority of his family in the tsunamai, and has rebuilt the hatchery. A lovely visit, thank you.
Not a very big place but definitely worth a visit. Get the chance to hold some on the turtles and learn something about them.

Myself and 13 other friends went to the turtle hatchery today and were instantly greeted by the owner. He then showed us the different turtles, with insightful information about their habitat, life span etc (but not too much info where its boring) then we were allowed to hold them, which was amazing. The hatchery looks out on an incredible beach too. The whole experience was so worth it! Perfect for children and adults. We are all aged 19-26 and absolutely loved it. You've got to go!

Two brothers' herculean effort to get back to mainstream life after loosing ENTIRE family in 2004 Tsunami. Themselves were saved as they had gone to Colombo for some work! Fighting the depression of loosing the loved ones, they showered their love on the turtles whose eggs are collected from beach to save them from humans & animals alike, who eat them. 3% natural survival jumps to 90% when they are released back into sea after attaining reasonable survival instinct. Even the big turtles having their paddle-legs cut-off by the nylon fishing nets or boat propellers or simply hunted to make jewellery from shell are nursed here and released back. The total fishes, molluscs and jelly fish needed to feed them daily is taken care of by entrance fee; The school children also visit to learn about turtles. GOD BLESS THE 2 BROTHERS.
Got the 388 bus to the big Buddha and spent 30 mins going round the sanctuary. It is a small place but very informative and great for the kids. You could combine with the tsunami museum.
My family and some friends went there for see the turtles .There was  so many sea turtles.. The owner explain about the sea turtles clearly . The place also cleaned and neatly.

My partner and I went to the turtle hatchery after jumping on a tuc tuc for something to do. We were not disappointed! Entrance fee 500 but this is due to the maintence and conservation of the turtles - it is a non profit organisation. There are various breeds and the owner provided us with an overview of the work that they do to conserve the turtles. Thoroughly enjoyed ourselves and we even managed to hold some of them including some recently hatched. A must see for adults and children alike !

My children (7, 5 and 4 yrs old) loved this. It's small and contains about 15 tanks with baby turtles and some with disabled old turtles. There is not much to it but the owner made a huge effort in telling us about the turtles and allowing the children to pick some up. We went on our first day in Hikkaduwa and the children want to ho back again on the last day to say goodbye to the turtles. The visit only takes 15 mins or so, so we're happy to do so and pleased to support the owner's (who lost many family members and the original hatchery in the 2004 tsunami) efforts.

We brought our 4year old daughter here. It's a great little place to spend an hour learning about the turtles and holding them. We had a lady that talked us through the various species. It's very cheap to go and children under 12 are free. Adults price us 500rupees which is £2.50
A nice small little setup where children would enjoy most, especially if they love animals and enjoy holding baby turtles in their hands.

Nice little place to see some of the turtles that have been hatched and rescued. The owner takes you through a short talk of the different turtles they have and after you get to pet some of  the smaller ones!! Good for kids or for a short activity.

From the top review's written on Tripadvisor I have honestly expected more. There are cca. 12 basins where are from 1 - 4 turtles (some invalids), except for the first basin where were only 1 day old turtles. Of course there are also many information about the single species on the wall. Initialy we have a 10 min introduction from the guy who is in charge of the hatchary, after then was difficult to get some other information, because the other guy didn't speak english as well. The hatchery is easily reached from Hikkaduwa with the local bus 388 (paid 20 Rp./person), but you have to exit immediatelly after you see the big buda statue erected after tsunami in 2004, because our bus driver didn't know where the hatchery is. Worth the visit also the tsunami museum over there.
See how this man helps the sick turtles back to health  and back to the sea hold the baby turtles my wife loved that part of the trip Visit is a must grab a tuk tuk and go see for yourself
Just been to the turtle hatchery at hikkaduwa its a small place with a big range of turtles. The guy there is very helpful and answered my questions. You can also pick up the turtles :)

This is close where the bus stops (bus 388) coming and going to Hikkaduwa, just north of the city. 500 rp entry with that you are allowed to access their wifi and see a number of baths that holds the turtles sorted by increasing age. You are able to toch and feel and we had the 'luck' that a few of these turtles had just been born. The guy who showed us around had a few interesting stories. The family history (Tsunami 2004) is impressive and humbling
Quite educational - you will learnt about the different types of turtle.  Good cause.  Small fee (500 SLR) to get into Hatchery.
the many disabled turtles show that people.in.the hatchery really care. Taking pictures is possible - with babies and big turtles

I likes the turtle project very much in an conceptual way and I did not regards leaving money there but its bit a pull cash from purse place and while partly interesting to see no must. bets part for me was I felt a bit helping the turtle else...

The map location on Trip Advisor is wrong. It is only about a 5 minuit drive north of Hikkaduwa, about where Google maps thinks it is if you search on Google. A good fun place to visit if your in Hikkaduwa. It takes about an hour to see, hear and read about all the turtles. Entrance fee is 500 Rs per person.

We came across the turtle hatchery by accident, but really pleased we did. The hatchery is run by a guy who is serious about turtle conservation and has dedicated his life to this. He has run the hatchery for many years, but sadly lost most of his family in the 2004 tsunami. The hatchery has been rebuilt since and is going strong. Locals buy turtle eggs to eat as there is a traditional belief that eating turtle eggs will make you strong. The owner buys the eggs to save them from being eaten- turtles are hatched there, and most are released back into the wild after a couple of days. The owner keeps a few to feed and strengthen them up before releasing them back into the wild later too. You can hold some of the smaller turtles, and there's some information about the different species. One side of the hatchery is a sort of retirement home for disabled turtles (lost limbs in fishing nets etc). Well worth a visit and good to support a worthy cause.
See cute little turtles only a few days old, what great little swimmers! Plus larger turtles being cared for before being released back to the sea, plus turtle eggs of different types.

This place is run by a really lovely devoted, inspiring guy, who was very open and willing to talk about the places history. He sadly lost family in the recent tsunami that struck the coast of Sri Lanka and the hatchery was completely destroyed. It has since been rebuilt from charity donations and is helped out by volunteers and donations today. The hatchery is well worth a visit, its only a small place but full of information and turtles of many different species and ages. There are some permanent residents there and other new borns that are hatched and then released into the wild. Allow for 40-60 minutes visit, well worth the short walk or rickshaw ride out of town. And all for support of such a great cause. I believe you can even volunteer with them if you have the time available and be sure to leave a donation after your visit.

We were staying in Galle Old Fort and travelled here on the bus, to hikkaduwa, which took about 30 minutes and cost 35rps each, each way. Then at the bus stop we took a tuk tuk which was only 3km away. All very easy and worthwhile to get to this amazing place. We feel thrilled to have had the opportunity to go and are absolutely beaming at having been to this incredible place. There are very old disabled turtles there, with missing or broken fins, then 3 different types of smaller turtles and tiny babies which were just one week old. You're able to stroke the turtles and they love it, as it tickles them. We were also allowed to pick them up. For anyone who likes turtles, this is an absolute must visit, not just for children, for every age, it's amazing and was an absolute highlight of our holiday in Sri Lanka. Entry to the hatchery was 500rps per person. Well worth every cent.

This place was better than I expected. We've been to other conservation places and they aren't half as good. It's a small establishment run by two brothers, formerly by their elder sister who died in the tsunami. It was established by their father however. This is definitely a place to visit as you learn about the turtles from the volunteers. You can even hold a few of them. It's a wonderful place with a good cause to help save the species.
We took some time to talk the to man who runs this great place.  Such a sad story he lost his family in the tsunami, but now puts all his energy into such a great cause.  Met this man and be inspires

First of all, get the GPS location from Tripadvisor/Google for "Kosgoda Sea Turtle Conservation Project" and store it in your maps. Secondly ask for Kosgoda tutle hatchery even if the tuk tuk/taxi operator drops you at Inaruwa or some other place. The 'real turtle hatchery' is run by a fisherman and few volunteers and is doing lot of things for turtle conservation. Unfortunately lots of imitations have come up which call themselves turtle hatchery which may not be contributing in conservation of turtles as the original one does. They will try to tell you things like "we have albino turtles which no other place has", take my advice, dont pay heed to them and continue heading to Kosgoda conservation area. Now coming to the place, the biggest highlight for us was being able to hold tiny turtles in our hands. One can see eggs/turtles in various stages of maturity, see limp turtle, humpback turtle, albino turtle, ticklish turtle & all 4 kinds of turtles

We went here and the kids loved it - they learnt alot about turtles and eels and had fun picking up the babies.  It was a nice stop on a day tour to various places, but wouldn't put it on the must do list for adults.

We visited the turtle hatchery this morning and I found the experience to be overwhelming. They really look after the turtles. They save them and nurture them back to sea,our guide was full of information which was so informative. We held the turtles which was surreal. Highly recommend

Worth a visit if your in hikaduwa, takes roughly and hour and a half. Various species of turtles are kept here in preparation for their relate back to the wild. The owner of the hatchery gives am interesting description on each of the types of turtle and the problems they face in the wild. You are also able to pick up some of the smaller ones, although be aware some of them may try to bite !
Nice for kids.. It take max 30 min.. We were happy to see the birth of a new baby!! Kids enjoy it.. But it isn't a must see for adults...

Was exciting to get to see them, not the best environment for the poor creatures but the owner is genuinely doing what he can for them, some were injured , others waiting for release. We got to hold the babies. Got a little tour and explanation of the work they're doing.

We visited quite late in the day and there was no-one around to give us the full tour but we were able to hold the smaller turtles which were awaiting release once the seas got a little calmer.  Nice place and worth a visit if only to support such a worth cause.

We enjoyed our visit to the turtle sanctuary. It is run by a gentleman whose family was tragically  affected by the tsunami. Turtles are brought to the sanctuary either as eggs or if they are caught in a fisherman's net they are brought here so they can be released safely. There are a few large turtles here that can't be released back into the ocean as they have been injured. The baby turtles are cute! You can pick them up but I chose not to as I wanted to leave them in peace. We were chatting to a family with young kids who visited the same time as us and they seemed to love it. There was a volunteer who gave us a wee tour with lots of information. It's worth going to see the turtles.
Was unfortunate.went there on off season but was able to see some. Was impressed with the attempt they are making.

We visited the turtle hatchery in june. There were only a few people,  because it was off season,  so we enjoyed our stay for 3 hours.  They had 3 day old turtles that we could pet and hold in our hands.  What a special feeling! They have lots of different types of turtles and some of  them are injured. The owner of the turtle  Farm explained that he will set them free again when they learned how to swim with 3 Flippers. Lovely place!
You can observe baby turtles and also older turtles here. This is one of the turtle farms in Sri Lanka. If you are visiting around Hikkaduwa, this is one place you must go and see.

This is a hands down must go if you are coming to Sri Lanka, the interaction with these creatures is just magical. The work that is done here is amazing and every little bit helps to give these turtles a fighting chance! Eggs are purchased from dealers who would otherwise be destined for the food industry. Eggs are brought to the hatchery to then be incubated and once hatched released back into the wild! Donations are welcome, there is 500 LKR entry fee! But goes to a good cause!

This is a MUST-DO!  The staff is warm and knowledgable.  You are up close & personal with baby, adolescent and injured sea turtles!  Beautiful experience.  The 'talk' is informative, interactive and short enough to keep kids' attention.  With a small donation, which we would have given anyway, we were able to hold an endangered species of sea turtle...awe inspiring for the whole family!  In my opinion, THIS is the way to motivate people to care for and respect wildlife & the ocean...not a water~theme park with a dolphin show or a zoo! VISIT THIS PLACE...NOT TO BE MISSED!

Loved the place but tripadvisor had given the wrong location ..ended up going 1 hour away although we did enjoy it he beautiful drive . This Hatchery is owner by a guy who lost his whole family during the sunami .really helpful and explained everything about turtles . This place is only 10 mins from Hikkadua center . It's a must visit .

My granddaughters aged 8 & 7 LOVED it! It was the highlight of their 2 week stay in Sri Lanka. The owner was very friendly & he had lots of facts & information to share with the girls. I was impressed as the aim is to release baby turtles after hatching & to strengthen injured turtles before releasing them back into the ocean. Turtle eggs are sometimes dug up & eaten so the hatchery buys the eggs at a good price to stop this practice.
Really enjoyed this visit, host was very friendly & gave lots of information we could all understand, privately funded facility which we gladly supported after our visit.
I enjoyed seeing the turtles and the host was very enthusiastic. He was obviously passionate about their future and was genuinely caring about the creatures.

Went here expecting to spend 10 minutes and was there for 1 1/2 hours.  This privately funded facility allows you to experience the full life cycle of a number of rare and endangered species of Turtle.  The staff are super knowledgeable and encourage the visitor to get "hands On". If you are anywhere near this place - you must put it on your :"to do" list.

Easy to get to by Tuk tuk from Hikaduwa.  A visit here will give any visitor a good understand about the importance of Turtles conservation. It relies on tourists for the upkeep of the hatchery and safe place for older turtle they care for. Very child friendly too.
It is a very small place but for children and animal lovers it still is quite a good place. There are many many turtles here and very old ones also.

There are a few of these places near one another. Entrance fee was 1000LKR. The tour shows you around the hatchery, right from the stage where the eggs are hatching through to fully developed turtles. They may let you pick up the smaller turtles. You can make an additional donation to support them.

We enjoyed our visit , very pleased to see how well the turtles are treated , we were met on arrival and taken round on a very informative tour of the different tanks where  the turtles were kept . I was pleased to see how well they were looked after and how clean everything is .

You will find there 5 different kind of turtles, from hatchlings to fully grown. Some local people dig out the eggs at night using to eat, but the owner buys the eggs from this guys for a pretty high price, place it in the sandy area within the conservation area and wait till the little turtles hatch from the eggs. Please support this as you can save a turtles life with you ticket or donation.
Amazing place to visit - one of the only place you can experience something like this
very informative ..and shows the importance of saving the turtles and how they protect it..good to take childrens along so they learn to serve the environment..

We recently visited this so called hatchery a few days ago. I was absolutely angered by the exploitation of these beautiful creatures. The eggs are gained illegally by fishermen and poachers to sell to the owner.  When we asked about how he obtained the eggs and turtles, he openly admitted that many turtle nests would have been destroyed by these poachers in the process of stealing the eggs to sell! I have never seen such cruelty and intervention of nature by these evil, criminal people. They pretend to protect the baby turtles but they allow the public to handle them. There are 5 species of turtles here, ranging from so called rescued eggs, baby turtles and larger turtles that should no way be kept in small stinking tiny tanks. These guys should be prosecuted by the police for cruelty to animals. If I had known this before entering, there is no way would I have funded these crooks by paying 1000 rupees each thereby helping to encourage such exploitation. I left extremely angry and upset. Please do not visit this place.  Let nature take its course - it is far kinder for the turtles to be protected on the beach and left well alone by mankind.

I really enjoyed our visit to the turtle farm. So much that I visited twice. You get to see the full story, from eggs through to release. I even got to spend some time helping Bob the manager do some releasing of the baby males back to the sea. I do question where all the females have gone? If they are breading 5,000 eggs per year, and 5% are female, my maths would expect to see more than 5 females in the hatchery

500 rs entry to see 5 -6 turtles. i think they are doing a good job of saving maimed turtles. need a better , more spacious environment. need to be more informative there were quite a few of such places on the route to bentota and they all looked similar.

These people buy the turtle eggs place them in a protected hatchery allow them to grow just a little then release them.  AWESOME.  They raise money through ticket sales and any donations.  PLEASE GO AND DONATE.
Small will not take you long to see everything but a worth while venture. The baby turtles are very cute. We were not there when they were being released but would love to see that.

This entry seems to be for both Hikkaduwa hatchery (according to the name) and Kosgoda one (according to the map) We were at the Hikkaduwa one. Very nice place, especially for small children. You can see and touch turtles. The host is very nice and gives detailed explanations about the turtles. Tickets for foreigners cost 500 lkr for adults. Return Tuktuk ride from Hikkaduwa beach cost us 500 lkr.

Have been volunteering here the past few weeks and can confirm that the turtles are treated very well. Every morning they are fed and each tank is drained and scrubbed once or twice a week. The government regulates the hatchery and they can only keep baby turtles a short 3 days before they must be released. The only turtles who won't be released are the three disabled turtles who would not be able to survive on their own. Each turtle gets medicine put on their wounds and their shells scrubbed daily. The owner is very knowledgable and it is a family run business. All of their proceeds go towards the turtles. They are very protective of their turtles and will not hesitate to escort people out if they mistreat the turtles. People are only supposed to take pictures with/handle the baby turtles, and they are supposed to do so respectfully and carefully.

You can learn here a lot about sea turtles and what these people do to protect them. As a real higlhlit you can pet them too - especially the baby ones. For 500 rupees it is one of the best experience we had in Sri Lanka.

It’s amazing the efforts made by this team to save the turtles. Good place to visit with the family, giving a chance to learn about turtles and how they've saved some after being injured from boats etc...

This place is small, but how big does it need to be in fairness? There are a few (4 I think) different breeds of turtles in the small years in separate large baths, with loads of tiny hatchings, slightly bigger babies, and a handful of full-sized turtles (who are too injured/missing limbs to be returned to the ocean). You can be in and out in a matter of minutes, but you won't leave before picking up one of the tiny creatures for a picture. This doesn't appear to be a tourist gimmick. The owner lost a lot when the tsunami hit, but he seems to be someone who helps the turtles in their circle of life.
Good place to visit with the family, giving a chance to learn about turtles and how they've rescued some after being injured from boats etc...
These people take good care of the turtles, they help in hatching the eggs, they feed them, help them in growing and then leave them to survive on their own. Visit and donate for a good cause.
A good short visit, very informative and you get to handle the turtles. They do very good work and help educate about turtles, so a good donation is welcome.
Very informative guide. Great that more turtles are able to survive due to this facility. Good tourist shop

The turtles are taken care by the people, the history of the owner's family is really a sad one, how he lost his entire family in the tsunami of 2004 and now he is taking care of the turtles, protecting them from sea monsters. We seen some handicapped turtles also and how he takes care. They are now trying to start full fledged with a good money. Entry fee is 500 LKR per head and iI would not regret paying even 2000 LKR if its for the good.
Amazing the efforts made by this team to save the turtles. One can also release the turtles into to sea for which you have to book in advance.

Interesting little place which is helping the turtle population around Hikkaduwa. The more people that come hopefully the more money they get and the more help they can give to the turtles. The owner seemed like he cares for the turtles and for a man who has clearly been through a lot it's good to be able to help him and the turtles.

It's a surprisingly small place, but really listen to what the man has to say and ask to hear his story... It is heartbreaking, he lost his family and everything in the tsunami and still he cares for the turtles, they are his mission in life. You don't often meet this kund of devotion, and of course the baby turtles are absolutely adorable, even they make it worrh a visit. I wish there was someone taking care of the dogs as well...
The work these turtle hatcheries undertake is amazing. Furthermore, later in the day whilst snorkelling, I was able to be able to see the turtles in the wild and appreciate them at first hand.

A small turtle hatchery that is worth a visit. There is a bigger hatchery about 30 mins from Hikkaduwa but this one is just a short tuk tuk ride away and close to the Tsunami Museum so a nice way to spend a few hours in the evening. A really nice idea and glad that the turtles are released as soon as possible. I would have liked to have released some but there were none being released when we were there. I wasn't overly happy with people being allowed to pick the turtles up for photos etc and felt they should be left alone.

We saw loads of these farms along the south coast of Sri Lanka, especially as we approach Bentota. As my son is an absolute animal lover, we decided to check this out on the recommendation of our driver as one of those things to do while on the coast of the country. We were given a tour by a guide who explained to us about all the 5 species endemic to the country, their life cycle, habits, etc etc. We toured around the tanks with turtles at different ages and also those who had disabilities and could not survive out in the sea (hence they kept them in the tanks). There are also sand areas marked with dates that stores the eggs they “buy” from the local fishermen in order to keep them from becoming food elsewhere, etc. The whole script is conservationist. However, I just have a feeling that these are all commercial enterprises exploiting the animals for profit under the disguise of protection and conservation. Why? Several times, the guide took the baby turtles from the tanks for us to touch and take photos with. In fact there’s a healthy grown turtle in one tank (weighting about 10 kilos) that was pulled out of the tank and passed from one tourist to the next for photos. I asked why he was there and he admitted that it was because visitors expected to see lots of turtles, hence they kept one adult healthy turtle at a time (and then rotated/ replaced them every three months). They also charge 1000 ruppees per person to release the turtles in the water later in the evening. Although this is only £5, for local standards this is a lot of money. The person there told me I would have to decide quickly before 4 PM if I want to come over that evening – anyway, a very pressurized sales tactic that I did not appreciate at all. Having spent a week in the Galapagos last year where they take conservation and animals really seriously, I can say that it is NOT ok to be touching and handling these animals the way these people are doing. I could see the turtles distressed every time they were picked up flapping desperately. Also, people come with dirty hands often smeared with sunscreen and bug sprays and is it OK to handle turtles that are less than 3 days old? They have a very nice speech of conservation, how they increase the survival rate, etc etc. The question is how dumb can you be to believe in the rosy story when all the evidence says otherwise. I wish I had read a review like this one before I went there.

We learned a few things about turtles and I guess he is doing a good job. I`m not sure, if I really believe that there are still people eating the eggs in the villages because we also heard that people stopped doing that a long time ago. But nevertheless, I think this turtle farm helps to have more turtle in the ocean and this is good! I watched turtles while surfing and that made my day :)

I volunteered at the hatchery for a month and had an amazing time. The turtles are so well looked after by staff and volunteers all year round. The hatchery has lots of information dotted around so you can learn lots about different turtles while you're there. I would recommend a visit.

We made a visit here with our 3 children. It was very interesting and the guy running it was very knowledgeable. We were able to pick up the smaller turtles which the kids loved but none were being released into the sea that day. There are some larger turtles that are injured and would not survive in the ocean that remain here permanently but the smaller ones are all released once they are big enough but only 1% survive apparently. The place was wiped out by the Tsunami and rebuilt by the current owners family.

Had a short visit here with my hubby. Not sure what to expect. The man running it told us what we needed to know and was available for questions. He relys fully on donations and the small charge we pay on the way in. His father opened it years ago to help the turtles. His father died after a sudden heart attack and his sister took it over. Then the tsunami hit, taking the hatchery, his sister, mother and other family. Him and his brother were working in columbo. The locals and tourists helped them to rebuild in 2006. When the turtles bury their eggs in the sand, it takes I think 40 days for them to come out and swim into the sea. 1 in 100 survive. Some people dig up the eggs before they hav a chance, and eat them. 😡. Some locals will bring them to the hatchery so they can be safe and released when ready. He doesn't have a huge amount of room but his idea is to release straight away. There is also a few large turtles that will be there longer due to missing legs or one had eaten a plastic bag. Common unfortunately as they think it's a jelly fish. So he keeps an eye on these to see how long they can stay under water and how they will survive when hopefully he can release them. There are diff types of turtles. There are some really small ones too that you can pick up. I didn't as I felt bad as they should be wild. Glad I saw and donated.
Stop by and see the great work they are doing to conserve the turtle population in Sri Lanka. Great staff who are very knowledgable. Worth a 30 minute stop!

Great little place to visit, turtles of all ages not just newly hatched. Some rescued turtles, but mostly young turtles getting ready to be released in the sea. Guide very knowledgeable, really interesting stuff. If you like that sort of thing.

This farm is located close to the beach, we went there and watch different turtles and got a chance to go to the beach and release the small baby turtles to the sea. It was beautiful time when many turtles are walking on the beach

Our two year old loved it, she got to pet turtles and see all kinds of different speices. We adults got an important lesson in the work they put in to protect the turtles of Sri Lanka (and we got to pet them as well). If you want to help releasing them into the ocean or see them hatch call ahead

I visited today before I headed back to Colombo and was so glad I did. One of the owners showed a small group of us around and explained the process from egg to to turtle. He also gave us some background information on how they rescue the eggs, care for them, allow them to hatch and then release the hatchlings back in to the sea. Highly commendable work and may they continue to help these amazing turtles. Thank you so much :)

This turtle nursery is not only a wonderful exercise in conservation but a lovely place to visit. The tour takes one from the time that the eggs are placed deep in the sand through to the time for the to be released into the sea. There are also large turtles, some of which have been saved after injury. A grand family visit. We wish the owners every future success in their attempts to encourage these wonderful creatures.
Don't expect exceptional things to see, but it deserves visiting and support. I liked the idea when my kinds buried the eggs in the sand... But you should be lucky to visit when they get the eggs.

Went there as it was recommended. Short 10 minute tuk tuk ride from hikka tranz hotel. Only 500 rupee entry fee. Got to take lots of photos and hold the turtles. We gave a donation but felt under no pressure to do so, which was a nice change from other places.
Worth a visit just to contribute to their good work.  Lots of little baby turtles ready to set free when the time is right

Amazing to see these beautiful creatures up close. The owner buys the eggs and helps them hatch safely as it is common for people to steal eggs from the beach. After a few weeks he releases back into the sea. He has some larger turtles that have some handicaps and has helped them but they are in very small tanks

Turtle eggs are a specialty for Sri Lankans and they still eat the eggs. The hatchery collects and buys the eggs and breads the turtles until they hatch. After raising them they are released to a protected area close by. They also have few injured, older turtles that cannot dive anymore (lost their fins to a boot propellor) and would die if left on their own in the ocean. Even though the pools are small for the older turtles the people take care of these turtles and saved them.

We visited this hatcher located near the Tsunami museum near Paraliya. It is a family run business that buys turtle eggs from sellers selling them for food, hatch them and release them. The place and the enclosures look very clean. You can see brand new turtles that they will release into the ocean. They also have some turtles that are older and they use for education and will be released eventually. Sadly, they have three turtles that are missing an arm and or a leg (likely from a motor board injury). They cannot dive below the surface and would not survive in the ocean.

Turtle hatchery only 10 minutes from Hikkaduwa. This is a small place, but I think the owner is doing his very best for the turtleeggs and for the injured turtles. I had a good experience here and would recommend this place :-)
It was all very cute and the staff were very friendly and informative. Plus we got an amazing sunset on the beach which was a bonus

Visited here one morning, you get to hold baby turtles, the guy who owns the place explains about the turtles and how his project works - they hatch and release babies regularly into the ocean and help disabled turtles learn how to dive so they can release them back, worth a visit for sure, I have a new found hatred for plastic bags too!

This is a volunteer and non govt funded organisation aiming at helping the turtles. When you see the injured turtles, it makes you emotional because you knwo humans have had a hand in their injuries....the people worjking here are so committed and happy to greet you and explain their work, that it should be a must on the journey near Hikaduwa....we enjoyed our 45 minutes there.....lots of success into the future.

We were made to feel very welcome to look around and take our time with all the turtles. The owner explained his work and we were educated on the different types of turtles and the dangers. Very informative and enjoyable. Would recommend This is close to hikkaduwa. Tripadvisor location is incorrect. You can find it on google maps.

We made 3 visits here, after the first time we returned at 6pm on 2 further occasions to help release the baby turtles into the ocean and wondered who would be there if any of them made it back to that beach in about 30 years time to lay their eggs. The man who runs this hatchery is so lovely. Please visit if you are ever in that area.
Spent an hour enjoying our time spent learning about the turtles. Our guide was great and taught us a lot. It was a very hands on experience...we were allowed to touch and hold. Had lots of fun.
These people do a valiant job to get more turtles back into the sea to lower mortality rates. Although the site is some sand pits with labels for eggs, and a few concrete tanks with turtles in.

The man who runs this sea turtle hatchery is doing an amazing job, releasing over 10,000 baby sea turtles back into the sea every year.  People along the coast dig up and sell or eat the sea turtle eggs; this hatchery buys the eggs at above market prices and then hatches and releases them.  The hatchery is very interesting to visit, and your USD $3.50 admission price supports their mission.  The real treat, however, is going just before sunset to help release the babies and watch them scurry off into the sea; an amazing experience!  Be sure to call ahead as they may not be releasing babies every night, and if you do go, be sure to give an extra donation to help their cause...

I was really impressed! We learned a lot anput the turtles in Sri Lanka and their efforts to ensure the turtles are hatched and returned to the ocean. I was surprised they let us handle the turtles (being Australian we are not allowed to do anything) but we really enjoyed ourselves here. We went with our 3 year old and in laws. We all had a great time. I would definitely recommend stopping in.

Fascinated by the close encounter and happy to meet the friendly guide. Enough information and sad to see how fishing and plastics make this place even more necessary. Being able to hold the babies was amazing.
Great to go here after the Tsunami photo museum (a couple of minutes walk apart). Baby turtles and adult turtles are adorable. The man who runs it is also lovely and inspiring.

We had a lovely visit, it costs 500rs to get in but well worth it. The guy who runs it is very good at answering your questions and you can tell how committed he is to this great conservation work. It's not a big place so don't expect to be spending a long time here-- up to an hour would be plenty of time to see the turtles and have a cool drink.
never thought we were going to be shocked at how many people stole turtle eggs great to have a guided tour from the owner so informative and caring
Had a lovely time here the project is funded solely by donations and is well worth a visit, the guide was good and informative.
Very suprice place. I loved it. I visited many turtle farm before, but tihi one wass best - frendly staff.
Had a perfect visit with family - lots of positive emotions. Staff are the real fans of turtles - exciting tour and details about turtles' life.
My wife and I visited this hatchery and found everything was well organised and informative. Prices for admission are reasonable. Recommended.

This facility is doing a fabulous job increasing the number of turtles released into the ocean, and ultimately increasing turtle population numbers. The 500LKR admin fee is well worth it, and the money is going to a great cause.

Had a good time seeing the different type and sizes of turtles at the hatchery in Hikkaduwa. We were encouraged  to touch some of the turtles, in particular the one that had lost flippers through being caught up in fishing nets, who responded so positively when rubbing their shell. On the day that we visited the hatchery we were fortunate to see a large turtle being released in the sea, now that it fully recovered from its injuries. The entrance fee was 500 Rupees for tourists and free to nationals, that is really worth it, especially knowing that this money helps those turtles. I would highly recommend this, especially if you do have young children, as it is a real learning experience.
beautiful turtles. Friendly organizers will tell you a lot things about turtles, also there are you can see small baby-turtles which you can take in hand

Whilst it was nothing to look at from the outside, the inside really highlighted the humanitarian side of both locals and gap year students. All of whom worked together in unison starting with buying the turtle eggs for a higher price than black market value, then storing them for their incubation period until they were big enough to be released back into the sea. For those that had permanent disabilities they tried to re educate them in order to enable them to survive back in the sea. If this was not possible they would keep them indefinitely. The Rs500 that foreigners were charged as an entrance fee all went to supporting the cause.  Ask when they will be releasing the next lot of baby turtles as visitors are allowed to go and watch. It was a great experience!

I visited in late afternoon and was educated about turtles by the owner.  The history of this establishment and the family of owners is very sad but hopefully both they and the turtles will have a brighter future now. I held a turtle egg and felt the turtle move inside, and I released 2-3 day old hatchlings into the ocean at sunset - a remarkable and very special experience.

Baby turtles... what more do you need to know? Go! If you go in the early evening just before sunset you might even get to release some new hatchlings into the sea. There may be moral issues about these places, but at least the turtles get to the sea rather than becoming an omelet.
The turtle eggs are collected and when hatched are returned to the sea, very informative visit and the staff get the message across how important it is to protect these lovely creatures.
It was good experience there, charging  rs  500.00 per person but they give you a tour with explanation

This was a nice way to spend an hour. A guy showed us around and explained everything to us. Yes, it is a bit sad and run down but it looks like they do care for the turtles. Got to hold baby turtles which was cool. Short taxi from Citrus hotel

Some of the reviews for this place worry about the conditions the turtles are in. Having been to a number of turtle places I think they've got pretty good space. Yes the big ones could do with a bit more room but they'll all be released when possible.the guy who showed us round was really knowledgeable and our kids loved you it. Won't take long to see.

This hatchery was only 10 minutes from our hotel and I thought it warranted a visited  because it seemed to discourage picking up turtles and turtle babies. Other hatcheries you pay to handle the babies and fully grown turtles which I think is totally unacceptable. Not sure now reading some of the reviews of this hatchery but certainly when we were there no touching was allowed. These are wild creatures after all. The hatchery is very small, we whizzed round in 15 minutes, but it was informative, and we got to see endangered turtles, although I do agree the tanks seemed small. It doesn't cost a lot to enter and we left a a decent donation so the good work can continue and to ensure that turtle eggs don't find their way onto the black market and end up in China where they are considered a delicacy which is horrid practice.

The place is rather small with bassins filled with small turtles you gently can hold in your hand. There are also larger older turtles in not that big bassins. Is that ok? Well if you want to tell about turtles on a minimum of budget, that probably is the only way you can do it. Its a great visit, and you kids will love it

In my opinion this was very average. That have approximately 7 tanks full of turtles they have saved from the oceans, in one sense they are doing a good service but in the other sense the ranks seem very small for turtles that have spent lives in the ocean. We didn't get to see any turtles hatching, you would be very lucky for this to happen during your time here.

Really hard place to review. It is a Turtler Hatchery after all. You can see turtles, younglings of them and take some pictures. Worth to visit on the way to tsunami museum, waterfalls or lagoon safari. This place charges 500 RS per person what makes it not really cheap one (it's the price of breakfast for example). I say it's worth a visit if you like the idea of Turtle Hatchery cause that's what it is)

The baby turtles were cute but there is no justification for keeping healthy grown turtles in tiny tanks. It was like a bad zoo. The  big injured turtles could hardly turn around. It would have been much better to concentrate on the little ones and give more information on life cycle, predators etc. I think the hatchery is doing a good job in releasing the babies but not in the way it treats grown turtles.

This is a lovely little place. They have turtles at various ages. They keep them until a bit bigger to increase survival odds. Normally I dont touch sea creatures as a rule buy if you put your hand in the tank the little omes swim on for the warmth :) They also have bigger turtles which have been injured in nylon nets...they are teaching them to swim down with three fins by putting the food a little deeper every day! :)
An organized and family inspired project to save and increase the turtle population.  Our 7 and 9 year old kids loved holding the 1 day old turtles.

Honestly, the people that run this are amazing! After a tragic start (which you can read about when you get there) they've managed to create a lovely, selflessly run hatchery! The workers are keen to answer any questions you might have in great detail, you can hold the turtles and if you go in the evening (5-6pm) you can release baby sea turtles into the sea! I can honestly say this was the best thing I've done whilst being in Sri Lanka! Would definitely recommend going!
A place to get close to baby turtles - it is not large but is readily accessible from Hikkaduwa by tuk-tuk. A small worthy place - do visit if you have any interest in turtles
this place is small but has maximum types of turtles , even you can find 1 day old turtles. best part is you yourself can touch turtles and have a close look into their habitat
You must go there at around 5-5:30 because at 6 or 6:30 in the evening you have a chance to set 3 days old turtles to the sea to set them free. It was one of a kind experience

We expected this to be a bit bigger even after we read some reviews its a about 30m2 in size and your welcomed by a guy saying "YOU GO 500RUPIES!" whilst ofcourse locals can go in for free they have a couple Of cute baby turtles and some poor older ones who will probably stay there till they die. The guide tells you something about all basins and what kind of turtle it holds expect a 10min visit

The first owner of this amazing institution was killed by the tsunami in 2004 together with almost his whole family. The place is now in the capable hands of the one son who were away from home when the huge wave struck. We were met by this person, who more than willingly informed about the hatchery and the work that is done there as well as a lot of facts about the different turtles. They live in tanks with water and food held as closely to nature as possible. Three of the tanks are occupied by big turtles recuperating from severe injuries until they can be released back in the ocean. In a big box lies eggs under heaps of sand til they are hatched by the sun's warm rays. The result can be seen in the tanks where mini-turtles swim around only a few days old. Other tanks have animals of different ages -- they can live until they are over 200 years old, the oldest weighing in at close to 200 kilos and measuring over two meters. Visitors are allowed to handle the rurtles with great care -- but watch out: There is a big one With a beak sharp and strong enough to take a finger off a careless hand. Come and visit -- and support the cause with a donation in the bos by the exit.
Great work is being done here - please visit and support. A chilling reminder greets you - the original proprietor and his family were killed in the tsunami. Now a son who was away from home runs it.
This was a unique experience. A small hatchery and rescue centre thag does some truly good work! Please come here and help support a great cause! It's really fun!!!

This is a really humbling place to visit after learning about the owners story you can view and learn about the various turtles waiting to be released into the sea. I really enjoyed seeing the turtles be fed and even have there pool cleaned as well as having the pleasure of speaking with the owner.
We went with our tour guild Ajith such a great educational time and so worth the visit and would recommend to all..

i loved this! cute little Turtle Factory run by a man who helps breed and rescue injured Turtles. you even have the opportunity to hold some. they provide you with information on the different types of turtles and the entry fee goes towards helping them. definitely worth a visit!

The venue is owned by a man that lost his family in the tsunami. He gave us some information on the turtles in his care. We even got to hold some of the turtles! 500 rupees entry per person, but this was definitely worth it for the experience.
If you never have held turtles in your hand, it is definitely worth it.  It would be even better if we could see them in their natural habitat.

The guy who runs this place inherited it after his sister who died in the tsunami together with the rest of his family. He buys the turtle eggs on the black market where they are sold to be eaten. He hatches the eggs and puts the turtles back in the sea. At the hatchery you can also see different kinds of turtles that he has decided to keep for various reasons. Around six-o-clock in the evening you can join him to release the turtles back into the sea (for 500SLR). All the entrance money and donations goes to maintenance of the hatchery.

It was absolutely heartbreaking to see large adult turtles kept in small ponds (1,5 square meter) where they can barely move let alone swim. The owner explained that he keeps them for 5 years for educational purposes (to show people) and then releases them back to the ocean. While he seemed to be knowledgeable about turtles and I suppose he does some conservation work saving baby turtles and releasing them back to the ocean I find it totally unacceptable that he keeps some (5-6) big adult turtles in these terrible conditions. When I kept asking him whether he finds the small ponds appropriate he got really offended and returned me my money. Also the fact that one the first things he offers is to take baby turtles in your hands tells you that it's more for a show than true conservation efforts.
Great tour and place. Such a heartbreaking story regarding thr owner and really shows his passion for turtles conservation. Amazing experience and we found it hard to leave

Spent a wonderful morning learning about the different turtles and their environment. The experience of being to handle these precious creatures was fabulous. The guide was very knowledgeable and professional. Also enjoyed purchasing a few souvenirs in the shop.

Absolutely beautiful! Great way to spend the afternoon surrounded by gorgeous turtles! You are allowed to pick up the littles ones, as young as two days old, and touch the others. The owner was extremely helpful, talking us through the different types of turtles they have and how he rescue and rehabilitates others. Definitely an essential visit!!
We loved the experience of handling turtles and the excellent intentions of the hatchery. The owner is friendly, well informed and passionate about helping the rate of turtles survival.
This place with soo many turtles that have been rescued hats off to the guy taking care of them he is a great human being after all that he has gone through salute! Place is a must visit Thank you

It is a nice turtle breeding spot, one of the many in this area.  I am not certain about the value it adds to conserving sea turtles.  The entry fee is a bit steep, and it does not feel like conservation organizations we see in USA.  Lonely Planet tags this place as the most commercial among all the turtle "sanctuaries" along the Colombo-Galle road.  I tend to agree with them.  My nine-year old daughter liked handling the turtles. Not sure whether we the tourists are part of the solution or part of the problem with all these turtle breeding centers and elephant breeding centers opening up in Sri Lanka!

The turtle hatchery was a surprisingly good outing for the whole family. The kids loved being able to hold and pat turtles. Foreigners pay 500r each but it was worth it to see the looks of pure delight in my daughters faces!

We chose to see this turtle sanctuary over the coral sanctuary based on tripadvisor reviews. The place did not disappoint. Our local guide was very knowledgeable on the process of how to take care of turtles from eggs to release into the water. He also had a great sense of humour which we really appreciated. It was    a very informative visit.

I am volunteering here for a month with Plan My Gap Year and so far I have had the best experience. Everyone has been so helpful and are really knowledgeable about the turtles. They are doing a great job at increasing the chances of survival for these turtles as well as protecting the disabled turtles who otherwise wouldn't be able to survive in the sea. You can tell the turtles are really well cared for. Definitely would recommend this place to anyone staying close by as its 100% worth it.

I am volunteering here with Plan My Gap Year for 5 weeks and it's been such a good experience. The people who work here do a great job looking after the turtles and teaching visitors all about turtle conservation. Would definitely recommend to anyone!

Volunteered here for 2 weeks in January. The team that run it are amazing. All the turtles are so well cared for and you can be certain that all the money from donations goes straight back into the project. I had such a good experience here and would reccommend anyone in Hikkaduwa to stop by for a visit. :)
So great to learn about and touch the turtles. These great people are doing great things for the preservation of the turtles.

They are doing a noble job ,they pick the turtle eggs ,hatch at the hatchery and put back the turtles in the ocean ,this way they are saving many lives.Kids love to see the life cycle of turtles and the information givens at this hatchery is very good.

Beautiful experience! They really care about the animals. The part when you can hold the turtules was interesting for all the generations in the group. The only catch is you pay at the end, but you can choose the amount.
The little turtles are very cute and the work they are doing to protect the species is admirable. Definitely worth the 500 rupies.
They have all sizes of turtles at the farm They have female & male turtles but some stories that they give are not digestible They have white turtles as weel & been in this work since many years

We visited the turtle hatchery to see the amazing job protecting the eggs and releasing healthy Turtles back to the ocean. The other amazing work was rehabilitating injured turtles and returning them. All by a team that lost so much in the tsunami.

I have been twice now, first time 6 years ago and then again in July 2015.  The staff are passionate about their work and you are given a very informative tour by a lovely chap who is full of energy and enthusiasm.  His English is fantastic and he really engages with visitors.  The work these guys are doing is fantastic and they really deserve support.  You won't be disappointed if you go here!
It is very nice place, to look to live of turtles. You can see in this farm tourtles from eggs to adult
Nice project to help the turtles. Good explanation about how they go about it. Short half hour enough to learn and have the kids hold and learn about the environment.

This was really nice to see, a small difference to a massive problem. Both brothers are very passionate about what they are doing. Unfortunately some visitors were asked not to pick up certain turtles which some people ignored completely! Please visit this hatchery it is  worth every rupee of the entrance fee and more.

This small place is run by a very knowledgeable guy who's passion for helping,save and protect the dwindling turtle populations is obvious as he shows you around this hatchery. The entrance fee is 500 rupees per person (about £2.50). You are taken to 'meet' the different species from egg to adult. There are some injured turtles who will never be released and you are told their sad stories. I'm not a fan of 'animal attractions' but I'm pleased we visited here.
It's small but definitely worth a visit! The guy who runs the place gives you lots of information about turtles and you can hold the babies. You can go by tuk tuk and we paid 300 return.
Great place, doing good work.  We were able to see the turtles at different ages and a few different species of turtles.  You are able to volunteer some of your time too to help.

Loved the turtle hatchery visit, its a place worth supporting. The owner showed us around the different turtles in the hatchery telling us stories and facts about the different types. The owner has a lot of passion about the place and is doing a really good thing for the turtles.
You can get out there very cheap with a tuk tuk and owner who shows you around has such compassion for these animals:) Also this hatchery has had a very hard past with the tsunami in 2004.

Just outside Hikkaduwa this place is run by a man who is doing what he can in a small way to educate people and help the survival of several of the world's most endangered turtle species. They pay locals for eggs which otherwise get sold to be eaten and then bury them in sand for the incubation period. Once hatched they are gradually released back into the wild giving them a greater chance of survival. There are tanks each with a different type of turtle in it and you really get to see the differences. There are also tanks showing the turtles at various ages from really tiny and you are allowed to hold those. Lastly there are a few tanks holding the rescued injured turtles which they are trying to teach to dive again. It is a quick visit and costs 250rs each. The owner is very informative and coming from a country where we aren't lucky enough to have these wonderful creatures in our seas it is a privilege to be able to see them so close up and get to hold them too. Worth a trip.
This gents family were wiped out in the tsunami.  He has rebuilt the turtle hatchery and dedicates his life to the protection of turtles. Lots of education with school children.
It's amazing. The man who works their has shown huge care for many animals. He is a real class act and you can see the love he has for turtles.

Not far out from Hikkaduwa town in a tuk tuk. We were shown around and talked through how they do everything by one of the people who runs it. We got to see lots of turtles of different ages and learned a lot. Well worth a trip for the money.
very interesting and able to interact with the turtles , different species of turtles and great information

Small nice place worth visiting for 30 minutes. Local people seem unaware that most tourist in my opinion don't want to eat the turtle eggs! These people are trying to stop it, it's even illegal to eat turtle eggs!
Good job the owner is doing. And the kids really loved getting to touch a turtle. Another tsunami recovery story.
Great work by owner to save turtles. Worth visiting to here the story how they work. The story about his father and the Sunami is terrible.

Amazing place to start the new year - releasing turtles into the ocean. Friendly informative staff, all providing a great experience. A must for anyone in hakkiduwa. Phone before hand to ensure you can release the turtles.

The owner of this turtle hatchery is very passionate about what he does; and even rebuilt the sanctuary after the tsunami destroyed it. There are currently three types of turtle to see here and we were able to pick up baby turtles. They also care for injured turtles here and teach them how to swim with their disabilities. Small centre, only need about 30-45 minutes here and well worth a trip from Hikkaduwa. Entry fee is 500rupees. I believe you can volunteer here also. The owner speaks great English.

Fantastic way to get up close and personal with the turtles from the babies to the full grown. The centre is fantastic and although the area is small in which they are kept it is clean and they are well looked after. Not to mention... HOW CUTE ARE THE BABIES!

We where delighted with the littlest of turtles right up to the more mature ones, our guide was informative and full of humor. We had many photo opportunities, and we got some great ones! but sadly lost our camera. Our 4 year old tried to pocket a baby turtle for a pet lol....lucky we caught him!

A great place to find out more about the turtles in this area. Hold a baby turtle, see how the disabled turtles are cared for and learn how you can support them further. Come early to watch the volunteers feed them, clean their shells and give them their medicine.
A good place to understand about turtles and their lives and also about human life.Great courage required after loss of family.We can see that in you.

We arrived to this place as an accident, we were just walking past coming from the tsunai museum. We enjoyed this experience and also the story how this turtles are kept there some time and then sent back too the ocean. Place is fairly small though.

This is a great place, the young guy that works there has very good English and has a lot of knowledge about the turtles that they clearly care about a lot.  They house 4 main types of turtles that are all endangered to some extent. All of the turtles here are common to the waters of Sri Lanka and have suffered at the hands of locals who eat the meat and the eggs. The hatchery offers money to the locals to bring the eggs to them where they hatch them, keep them until they are 4 years old to give them a better chance of survival in the wild and then release them.  They also house some sick and injured turtles who they nurse back to health before releasing. The hatchery makes money by charging people in and through donations, though ultimately it is not set up as a tourist attraction.  If you want to bring your kids to see animals perform in pristine tanks then I would suggest Sea World or something similar. They do good work here and obviously care about the turtles.  If it was not for the efforts of places like this it is unlikely that you would have the chance to see any wild turtles on the reef off Hikaduwa beach! Good work guys, keep it up!

A must visit.they are doing a great job...specially the guy uwith the tattoos who took us around.....speaks good english and has a good knowledge about the turtles.......we had fun.....good job again...........

Visited today.  500 Sri Lankan Rupees entrance fee to see a small number of tanks in a small space.  Some tanks were empty - presumably for hatching.  Some had just one or two small turtles in.  Others had large turtles, two of which were desperate to try and climb out of the side of their tanks. I am sure that this hatchery was set up with good intentions, but the impression I was left with was that this was simply a way of making quick money from tourists. I chose this to take my non-verbal son to show him turtles, instead I left after about 2 minutes having seen enough.  We later saw turtles on the shore in the more touristic area of the beach in Hikkaduwa - which was a much happier experience.
Great time, you can try to keep turtles in the arms! Thanks for the interesting time spending and for a new feelings. The guys are very friendly and good.

They really do good thing for saving turtles, however, you must expect that they will emphatically ask you for some donations, even though you have already paid for the entrance ticket. I personally expect it to be bigger and more impressive. Small place, 15 minutes is enough to visit it.
This place is amazing you see everything from turtle eggs, 1 day old hatchlings to blind and disabled turtles. This place also has the only albino turtle in the world. It is well worth a visit
A very good job being done at this hatchery! Lovely to see turtles and learn their lifestyle! Great work being done in preserving aquatic life!

this was a good attration as found out lots of information about the turtles and also the cruelty that takes place, which was sad. However, the turtles seemed to be well cared for and in big tanks and the man took his time to explain about the different breeds and the rescue turtles he has. We also got to see some hatchling released!! Would recommend.
This was a good stop to see the turtles. It was lovely to see the different types. The hatchery itself is quite small so we didn't stay very long.

I spent a few weeks back in 2013 volunteering my time to help out Nimal with the hatchery; renovating, cleaning tanks, and online marketing, and it's truly great to see him and the turtles doing so well this time round. Definitely a worthy stop if you're passing through with knowledgable guides to teach you about numerous species of sea turtles, experience them during different life stages, and learn about their local conservation issues. Nimal, his family, and team are extremely infectious and you honestly feel and see where every penny of your small donation fee goes! This cause is definitely setting a positive mindset not only for the passerby but for the local community also. I can't recommend this little gem enough!

Just outside the town of Hikkaduwa there is a hatchery. This one isnt the best but still worth a visit. There is a better one in a town called Kosgoda. However the work they do is the same so if youre interested of turtles and their life its a easy reached place.

We went here on a rainy day as it was pointless going to the beach and we are glad we did. You learn so much about these amazing creatures, including the 6 different types, their lifestyle and characteristics. We saw rescued turtles with lost limbs, picked up ones 3 days old, saw eggs and the staff amazed us with facts and happily answered every question we could fire at them. Poachers follow turtle trails to steal their eggs to sell for 'medicine' but this charity buys them and then rehabilitates them back into the wild.
