As mentioned in previous comments they don't push for donations but you know what a good cause they are doing that you want to.

We went there to see the baby turtles and bringing them back to the sea. It was really nice experience, also knowing that you are helping the turtles. The place was very small, but the owners were really nice and telling a lot of the turtles. After that she gave us a bucket and we could bring some baby turtles back at the sea, so birds cant eat them. I really liked this place and I would go there again.

The guide here is very polite and sweet. He patiently answered all my questions and showed me around. The new born turtles are really cute and its just amazing to see so many of them together...! You start the tour from seeing the different turtle eggs, then the babies, females and males and the ones who have been injured and the highlight is the Albino Turtle (extremely rare). You can even carry some of these turtles. There is a souvenir store inside the hatchery, though a little expensive, they have some really nice products. There is no entry fees for the hatchery, however you will be expected to make a donation as this is completely funded by donations. Over all a fabulous experience!

I was here in 2013 during my first visit to Sri Lanka and ended up helping Nimal to renovate the hatchery. Over the years since I visited damage from storms occurred and much work needed to be done to fix the place. Through hard work and great support from tourists, the local community and conservation organisations the hatchery is now in great shape. Please support this great cause and help the family running the conservation project by visiting the hatchery. The staff are very informative and are more than willing to help answer your questions. A must if you are visiting Hikkaduwa during your visit. It's about 300-400Rp in a tuk tuk to the north of the tourist part of Hikkaduwa.

We loved it here, the man saves so many turtles and tries to nurse them back to health to release them back into the sea, he is even in talks with the government to get artificial limbs for the ones who have lost theirs in the fishing nets. It's a lovely, small sanctuary and you get to hold a few of the friendly turtles as well

This sanctuary is doing an amazing job at rehabilitating hurt turtles (endangered and not) but needs funding as no gvt funding is available. Held a 1 day old turtle in my hand. A must see when visiting Hikkaduwa. The Rs500 entrance seemed arbitrary in the face of their good and honest work.
We were very happy to visit this place, you get to touch the small turtles and even bigger ones. We had a very nice guide and its a very good conservation program.

Woke up this morning to rain and decided to go visit the Turtle Hatchery to while away the time. After reading the reviews on TA this seemed to be the best reviews. Our private driver hadn't been before and was a bit hesitant about us going but afterwards he told us it was the best he had seen. The place was clean and tidy, the person showing us around the facility was genuine and was passionate about his job. We were not expecting to be able to hold or touch the turtles which was a nice surprise. Would recommend going, worth the 500rp charge.

Important work preserving the turtle population in Sri Lanka. 5 different types of turtles eggs are being preserved here protecting them from predators  (mainly human). Before hatching. There were over 1000 eggs being looked after helping to save these turtles from extinction After hatching the turtles are looked after for a few days before returning them to the sea. The hatchery is quite small but the message of conservation is what really powers through here.

Turtle Hatchery, is a very nice place, a more educative tour which makes us realise that even Turtles are part of our earth & how much they contribute towards the balance in nature. Only 20% of the eggs survive till the end. The staff are very much dedicated towards taking care of every minute detail with regards to eggs & the newly hatched turtles. There is a shop which sells few articles which directly contribute towards the turtle hatchery foundation.

The people here do a very important job. Unfortunately turtle eggs are seen as a food source, and of course that means turtle populations are declining. This small centre recovers eggs before they are "stolen" from their nests, hatches them and releases the baby turtles into the ocean. They also take in injured turtles and release them back when recovered. Fantastic and humbling work that should be funded but is not, they rely on people visiting and making contributions. It's a great cause I'd contribute to anyway. But as a visitor you will see baby turtles, so cute (you may get a chance to hold one too). You will see some adults of different species of turtle and be educated in their differences, also in the ways they are harmed by humans. And don't fail to ask about the tsunami, this place was wrecked but has been rebuilt and reopened through dedication and hard work. I have nothing but praise for the people who run the place.
Very moving to see how much the staff genuinely cared for the turtles. Very educational. It felt really good donating money to their cause. Our daughter loved holding the little baby turtles.

The local turtle farm of Hikkaduwa takes care of different species and helps to prevent extortion. These volunteers gave excellent info about the lifecycle of every turtle they have, why they are in the farm and when they go back into the ocean. We even saw and got to hold little turtles from only 7 days old. Super cute!

Built on the foundations of the tsunami disaster, the hatchery is definitely worth visiting and supporting. I have firsthand experience of the workings of the hatchery and know for sure that the staff are dedicated to their job and to conserving this endangered species. They care about each turtle and about repopulating the sea with them (which they're doing a very good job at). Disabled turtles are looked after and rehabilitated until they can be released into the sea, given medicine and a chance to recover after being harmed. They do great work in acquiring eggs that would otherwise be sold on the black market and are reducing the amount of turtles and eggs eaten. In addition to all this, it's a really nice visit and to see such amazing creatures first hand is incredible.
Very informative staff are very knowledgable and tell you about the different species of turtle they have.We held a 3 day old green turtle which was cool.

By visiting this place you become a part of a great project for a good thing. They help to handicapped turtles and take care of the baby turtles. You will meet different kinds of turtles and get a lot of interesting info. Sure this place needs more money and more investments to get better conditions for the turtles.

We were so happy to see the hard work these guys do for Sea Turtles. They rescue, treat and release wounded turtles, and they help to stop locals eating turtle eggs so they can hatch them and release them later instead. We also got to hold baby turtles that had hatched only the day before, so it was definitely a memorable experience!
This is a rather small place, but the enthusiastic guide gave us a very good description of the life cycle of the turtles and the importance of preserving them.

Looking at the turtles of all ages, from the hatching to the age off 55 yrs and beyond, and of all sizes that fit within your palm and some which are not even possible to lift, is the most amazing hands on turtle experience I've had yet. Will recommend all families travelling with children to must visit the Turtle hatchery
Our kids really enjoyed the visit, very good explanations, friendly staff, overall happy and satisfied.

the hutchery gives an opppotunity to get close to sea turtles, especially the baby ones. You can see them from very near by, and (not officially allowed) even touch them. This makes it a very nice experience. the hatchery itself is small and explanation is limited.

What an experience, those turtles are really loved and cared for by all the staff, who are so knowledgable about the turtles! I 100% recommend you to visit the sanctuary, right on the coast with lovely views too and a great little gift shops. They let you pick up the turtles  and tell you all the individual stories of the bigger ones they've cared for some years.
So nice to see ...you will Oooo and Arrr thought our your visit and they do a great job looking after them all .

The rescue centre do a great job for sea turtles. Here you can seedfferent types of sea turtles and their eggs. Baby turles are put out to sea when they are three days old. Turtles that are borm ,blind,or missing aloafer will stay in the hatchery for life which i a good thing. Well worth visiting !!
So sweet ....one day old simply loved them! The staff here do a greart job here. Had to go back again  to see these baby's

The turtle hutchery is a nice place, they reall help the turtles. the pay the locals people money for bringing the eggs to them instead of eating them. you can touch the turtles - the bigger ones stay there for 5 years until they are released in the oean. entrance fee is 500rp.

One of the best things to do and you really get to see the turtles up close and personal. My tip would be to spend lots of time than most do at each tank and you can see the different attitudes of each turtle. Great company and lots of helpful volunteers working at the sanctuary.

A little home to many turtles including the 8-year old Albino turtle. Turtles hatch, are fed and taken care of. When they grow up, they are released into their natural habitat. The caretakers (many of them volunteers) allowed us touch and hold the turtles in our hand. Amazing work these guys are doing, I was so touched.

We were taken here on our way to Galle, What an incredible place. Eggs are buried on site after being brought in or their location being identified by locals. You will see lots of baby turtles and get to hold some larger ones. The hatchery we visited had a albino turtle, which was very rare. Not sure that the whole system here is perfect, but it obviously saves young turtles from being stolen and ensures that they at least reach the sea. They look after injured turtles which are brought in by the public. Given the limited resources these hatcheries have, they do a really great job. There appears to be no fee, but they are very keen for a donation after seeing and holding the turtles. Then you are shown to the gift shop.

There is lot of variety here and some of the biggest turtles I have ever seen are housed here. There are 3 hatching fields here and 100s of hatchlings around! But this place needs more funds. Needs to be better managed. We took an entire tour by tagging along with another group for FREE! Since its being run for a good cause, we contacted the manager and paid voluntarily. Serious lapse in management.
beautiful place with a beautiful cause. saw baby turtles. also saw turtles with broken arms and legs. really appreciate what the owner of this place is doing for the turtles

An informative journey and learning experience about the 5 different turtles that comes to shore in Sri Lanka. The owner explains the cycle from how to hatch an egg right through to releasing baby turtles back to the sea. There are different species of turtles in the centre and visitors are able to hold and touch them..   Please visit and contribute if you can.. together we can save more turtles and educate the public not to eat the eggs or kill the turtles

Great opportunity to see baby turtles up close. You can even hold the 3 day old ones.  The guides give you a very detailed explanation of what they are doing at the hatchery- everything from releasing baby turtles to rehabilitation for injured or deformed turtles.
very good educational tour of different types of turtles..eggs to adults different stages. kids loved it..u can hold the baby turtles in yr hand

We visited the turtle hatchery during the evening time after Madu river safary. This place has a nice collection of different types and ages of turtles. Guide shared very useful info and described each and every type of turtles and how thery are different from each other and they have been conserved. The place has an entry fee of 500LKR per person. The guide will allow you  to hold hand take picture with turtles. Over all a nice experience. Recommendation:- Please visit during day light to have a better experience and spent around 30-45 mins. Take a tuk-tuk for the ride from Hikkadua. The road ride is amazing

These people do amazing work rescuing turtles. They take eggs from local fisherman and bury them in their hatchery and release them to the sea once they have hatched and grown enough. Here you will learn a lot about turtles from the friendly guide and you get to hold turtles if all ages, from 2 weeks old right up to 25 years old. The turtles are beautiful. This is not to be missed with the family if you are in the area. Grab a tuk tuk to drive you there for an even better experience.
The owner gave an informative tour around the hatchery. Nice job to see someone so passionate about their role in helping the turtles.
Barely enough to see, spend twenty minutes on way to your destination beach. It's good contribution towards preservation of environment.

I am not sure about this Hatchery, yes it is helping to save the Turtles but to keep the Larger Turtles in such small ponds which looked as if they had never been cleaned was a little worrying as was the lack of water, just enough to cover them.    I was upset of see Baby Turtles being handle by the Public as very the Larger Turtles.  We were not asked to wash hands or wear gloves therefore germs were being passed on to them, yet we were asked to wash hands after handling (just don't know). Pleasing to see people are trying to do something but Sri Lankian Government could be more active.
Many beautiful turtles from fry to large disabled after shark attack. Kept in excellent conditions on donations.

A good place for hands-on experience with the Turtles. Up and close with them. Click some pics. Huge turtles to witness and learn their life cycle. Most of them are injured and on recovery stage. A good place for a quick visit without wasting much time. They charge money from foreigners. You will need maximum 20minutes for this place.

Informative although small site. The guy running (& living at the site) has a trajectory story as his father set up the project and when he passed away his sister and family took over. The Tsunami tragically struck and his family were taken. He has made it his life to run the project. You can handle the small turtles and the tanks are quite small for the larger disabled turtles but the space is limited at the location. Overall well worth a visit and we went twice.

We found this centre when we were visiting the tsunami memorial which is very close by. Entry cost 500rps per person. The place has been here for a long time and is doubtless run for the benefit of thr turtles. The owner is explained (in good English) that he often brought the turtle eggs from markets to prevent them from being eaten and brings them back to the sanctuary to hatch. When they are appropriately sized they are released into the wild. The baby turtles are housed in large tanks and can be handled and photographed. There are a number of full grown turtles in what appeared to be small tanks on display. The manager also looks after fully grown turtles that are injured. (Several had damaged flippers) Although I profess to know nothing about sea turtles I was concerned that the tanks for the fully grown turtles appeared to be too small. This is not an indictment of the management as the clearly care deeply about the creatures and are doubtless doing a good thing by rescuing and nuturing the turtles.
I was lucky - a baby turtle had just hatched. Is was also a hospital for injured and sick turtles. Very caring staff
Its the only place where you get up close to Turtles, their life cycle. You can learn all about turtles. Also get a chance to photo op with these beautiful creatures. A learning experience indeed.

Before the tsunami disaster, this was there and now they are helping to many more turtles. Last time when I went there they had around about 200-300 turtles. People in here, doing a very hard work to protect this little creature for the future without any donations from responsible parties.

So sad to see the larger turtles confined in a very small pond with a  low level of water. For some this is how they will spend the rest of their lives and you have to wonder whether it would have been better to let them die. tThe hatchery is doing what it can to save many  baby turtles and relies on entry fees and donations so there is the hard sell and pressure to give more.
We had a lovely time here. We got to hold the turtles and even the baby ones which were only a few days old.
Good effort by locals to run a charitable conservatory. Saw 5 types of turtles. The entry fee for foreigners is high.

First time to visit Turtle Hutchery Farm. The owner have a very sad background after he lost his family in Tsunami. An close experience with sea turtles, can feel the solf eggs, baby sea turtles, adult turtles, and some handicap turtles after rescruced by the team. Please do your donation, because this is non-profit organization.
I will always remember the wonderful time spend at Turtlw Hatchery. The stuff is really nice, turtles are extremely nice, you can play with the little turtles. Wonderful experience!!
A bit out of Hikkaduwa on the main road close to the Tsunami memorials, get up close to baby turtles and see how they help injured turtles.

We noticed this when we went up to see the Tsunami memorial where the train passengers died. Its between the memorial (Buddah statue) and the  Tsunami photo museum a little further up the road in Paraliya.  Its a  bit smaller in set up in comparison to the Kosgoda hatchery but the location makes it very easy to visit from Hikkaduwa. The staff (2 Sri Lankans + a number of western volunteers) were very helpful, spoke good English etc... There are the posters explaining the life cycle of the turtles, the threats to them, the types of turtles found in Sri Lanka but no shops like Kosgoda. However as we appeared very sweaty having walked up from Hikkaduwa we were ushered over to the a small low table and chairs with views out to sea through a mesh window (which had an artificial border pained around it to make it look like a massive flat screen TV) and provided with a ice cold 2 litre bottle of coke from somewhere to cool down before the tour started. Friendly and relaxed.  It was R500 a person so the same price as the other Turtle Hatcheries. They have the big marked sand pits with the eggs under nets the multiple concrete tanks for the baby turtles that are released at 3 days and few older turtles and injured turtles that were being kept until well enough to be released or permanently if they had lost more than one limb. Like the other turtle hatcheries they let you hold the babies but no flashes.  The babies get released at 6.30 each day (if they have babies to release) but they vary the location a bit so as to not encourage predators. There were 3-4 other larger turtles there too which they explained they keep for a while and then release so that there is more diversity for the tourists to see, which sounded credible rather than a denial they they all needed to be there This place had apparently been around quite a while although several of those who worked there dies in the Tsunami. There is a reasonable website with some pics. Not crowded, relaxed and they fed the little ones when we were there Well worth a visit, oh and decent western style loos.

This is a must see if you are in the Hikkaduwa area. The owner has taken on a task of changing people's perceptions of turtles in Sri Lanka from a common animal to an endangered one. He does a sterling job  of teaching local school children. The business and the turtles need patronage and 500 rupees per head is very reasonable. Well worth a visit.
This is a wonderful place, hundreds of tiny turtles hatched and safely taken to the sea. If you are lucky you can carry some into the surf.

Really lovely sanctuary set up by a man with an incredible back story about his survival through the civil war and tsunami. Sanctuary itself is basic and turtles are quite crowded but there survival chances here are a lot higher than in the sea. We were allowed to pick up the turtles and take pictures with them. entry is 500 rupees (about £2.50). If interested in turtles also head down to hikkaduwa beach as there is a man who coaxes in wild sea turtles with sea weed and he let's you feed them and stroke them ect.
it is great place to see the turtle in your tour to south coast of the country. Sea turtles being given life in those hatcheries

This was a nice and short visit. They are buying stolen turtle eggs from people and hatching them and feeding them so that they one day can be released in to the sea, witch is very good. It was fun to hold the small turtle that was only one day old.

This a small place located just before the busy tourist area of Hikkaduwa. The entrance fees were reasonable and for tourists it was only LKR 250/-. This place is actually a conservation center for turtles and a care taking place for injured turtles. The cute little turtles were adorable and can spent quit a time looking at there aquatic skills. Well, its a small place and you don't have much to look around. Just turtles in cement ponds and small area for hatchery. Overall a unique experience to get closer to an endangered ocean beauty.

It is possible to see turtles in different  sizes at the hutchery.  You can pet and hold the turtles too. An employee will guide you around. It is very visible that the employees love their turtles. Admission fee is 500 rupis for one person.

I have to say, this visit has been the best one in sri lanka, better than all safari, dophins and whales cruise, Pinawella etc. You can finally see really organization which just want to help and not make money. Turtles are so cute and you can also cuddle with them:).. My favorites were blind ones (easy to take a good photo cause they don't move so quick) and albino turtle - it's really rare (check my Instagram for photo "peli16"
Such a nice visit! The turtles were so cute and the staff very nice and friendly, they ordered us a tuk tuk as it was raining. An excellent way to spend a morning!
was a lovely experience. got the chance to see small turtles and also the guys over there explained about them.. A must visit place. Cheers

Kids can't stop talking about this experience.  They did not want to leave.  Sad to see effects of humans on these beautiful creatures, but great to see the efforts made to make a mends.  A real sanctuary..

I loved the fact how much I learnt about turtles. You can hold the very little ones - I was very lucky I went there on a day the little ones hatched. The guide let me carry one little one from the sand to the tank and then he gave me a year old one - around 5 kg! I have an amazing life experience which I will never forget. And the entrance fee is RS500. Go have fun and support local turtles!
We really enjoyed our visit here the staff were very knowledgeable and spent time teaching us about turtles.

Super knowledgeable guide who gave us a lovely insight into the work of the sanctuary. We were lucky enough to have the place to ourselves and were able to ask lots of questions and get up close and personal with all the different turtles. It's a lovely thing to do if you're in the area for sure.

Conservation of turtles have returned 30 million hatched turtles to the sea, the program is run without governmental aid by volunteers, four or five types of species on display here. Not many facilities, sandy area so difficult for wheel chairs or strollers. There is a small souvenir which has articles representing the hatchery and Sri Lankan beaches.

It is a rather small place on the main road in Peraliya, Hikkaduwa. This hatchery was formed to protect Turtle eggs that were laid on the shore and to provide shelter to injured turtles. Since Turtle eggs & meat are illegally consumed & sold illegally this task become so much more difficult. Once the baby turtle are of age they are released back into the sea. Entrance if free to locals however, Rs.500 is charged from foreigners. There is also means of making donations towards this cause. They also take volunteers to help with the day to day chores and cleaning of the tanks etc...The current owner has continued to operate this hatchery even after great personal loss after the Tsunami in 2004 affected his family as well as the hatchery. It is quite educational and an interesting experience to identify the 4 types o turtles and also hold the baby turtles.

The hatchery itself is just a small sandbox with eggs and several concrete baths with different types of turtles - nothing much to look at. There is a little information on the signs by some of the baths, and the place owner provides some additional information verbally. At the same time, the story of the hatchery owner made me feel good about visiting the place and paying for quite an expensive ticket (500Rs). The guy is buying turtle eggs on the black market and puts them to hatch in order to bring them back to sea. He's also taking care of several disabled turtles.

The people running seemed to care about the turtles.Also there was also an albino turtle. Some turtles were without flippers damaged by fishing nets.I guess they are doing a commendable job.You can do voluntary work at the hatchery.
Hutching happens only night-time (on the beach); and disappointingly, requires a separate guided tour and fee. Only different types of turtles in various age groups were on display at the Hutchery.

This turtle hatchery is 'low key', it has the feel of a personal project of a family's aim to protect these lovely animals.  It is a long-way off being a 'tourist attraction', thank goodness.  I hope that it stays true to its cause. The family background is that of a tough history, illness and sudden death of the founder, tragic loss of life (and the hatchery) through the tsunami in 2004.  But the brothers fight on with dedication and commitment. We visited once, by chance, on a mini tour (just by tuk tuk, 1.5km from Hikkauwa) to see the tsunami memorial, Buddha and tsunami photo museum (all near-by)....we stayed nearly an hour that day...mesmerised by the information given by one of the brothers. ...of course holding and watching these creatures is a very special treat for children (and adults). We returned the next day again and spent longer, with no other visitors we were made most welcome and sat chatting more informally with the other brother...who is an inspiration. We paid just 500 rupees/person to enter (£2.50/$3.50) but there is the option (no pressure) to make a further donation if desired.  Well worth a visit (and a donation).... ...We were chatting with the brothers about 'gap year students' who have recently helped-out at the project....Guess where our kids want to go when they are slightly older!

This is a great little excursion where you can see and touch the turtles at different stages of growth. Our guide was extremely knowledgeable, and we were able to see various different turtle breeds. We also saw disabled turtles, born blind or disfigured who are cared for in the sanctuary. Also turtles injured by motor boats or nets. My son enjoyed picking up a 3 day old baby turtle. All in all, a lovely experience
The turtle hutchery is formed after the tsunami in 2004 to save the regional  turtles kind . It is consist of different tanks to rais baby turtles and release them in the sea after 3 to5 years

Make sure you speak to the old man behind this hatchery. He has some amazing stories... Very educational visit with hands-on experience... it inspired the kids to even volunteer for this great cause... learned a lot...

This guy does a fantastic job to save the eggs of the turtles before they hatch. The locals dig out the eggs and sell them for a few ruppees, but this guy buys them at a higher price and consequently saves turtles.

We learned a great deal. They explained the whole process of how they get the eggs to where they release the turtles.  You get the hold some of the baby turtles, it is great for kids to visit this location.  I would highly recommend it !

It was nice to see and hold the small turtles. By passing the different pools you were able to se a turtle from one day old up to several years old. It was a nice and quick visit with good staff how answered every question in a professional way.
chilled place , there was many turtles of all sizes to look at a very interesting place to spend a few hours
make a point of going, ask if you can release some and for a small fee you can help the little turtles go. something you will never forget.

We found this place interesting as the guy showed us round, explaining all about the types of turtle there. He said that poachers steal the turtle eggs and sell them on the black market, and he doesnt like this (Although he buys the eggs from them, i found this confussing). There is a turtle there who has eaten a plastic bag and can never dive again, which was a little upsetting.

We experienced a very nice personal tour given by an intern student from the UK. See various species of turtle at different ages and cast your eyes on protected areas of sand where egg batches have been carefully buried pending the "big hatch". Small yet charming and not expensive. Nice place for a 30 minutes stop.

You never know if these places are just scams for making money, I do hope not. At 500RS it seems a bit expensive for what you get but you get a guided tour of the small establishment which displays different types of turtles you can expect to see in the oceans around Sri Lanka. These creatures are so cute and you get to handle different size ones too. The money raised goes towards buying the eggs off the locals that find them on the beach and are ready to make a turtle egg meal from them. So not sure if it saves them from becoming a meal or just encourages them from being dug up from the beach, hopefully not the later. Would I go again, probably as I am ever the optimist and would like to think this is an establish that is there to try and protect these beautiful creatures.

This is a lovely little local run attraction. They hep conserve the turtles, allowing them a few days of safety before being released into the sea, they also rehabilitate or care for injured turtles. It is a shame that the actions of people have rendered these establishments necessary but they have. Visit, your entry fee will help support this worthwhile initiative.

The visit to the turtle hatchery was one of the highlights of our Sri Lanka holiday. The enthusiasm and devotion of the staff and owner was amazing, they really have the turtles survivals close to their hearts. The care and devotion they give brought a tear to our eye, it was amazing. The care and attention they give to injured turtles is heart warming and we were only to pleased to contribute a donation for their care. The staff fully explained to us how the fisherman pick up the turtle eggs from the beach and sell them to the hatchery, this ensures that predators and humans don't damage or destroy the egs on the beach. The hatchery then hatches the eggs in sandpits  before caring for the young turtles for a few days before releasing them to the sea. We were lucky enough to have privilege to release 10 baby turtles into the ocean at sunset, a truly magical experience! To ensure "our" turtles made it, we ran backwards and forwards along the beach chasing away a sea eagle! Hopefully our turtles will grow old gracefully!
I liked the care and dedication with which the staff tended to the baby turtles, the eggs and the injured adults.

We was in Hikkaduwa turtle farm, ticket 500 rupees, 100 m from Tsunami Buddha statue by main road to Colombo side. It's not very interesting and small. Maybe in Kosgoda Sea Turtle Farm more interesting. For me more interesting big wild turtles at Hikkaduwa beach. We also saw how release small turtle on this beach.

I visited this place since I had heard a few good things from friends who had been here earlier. I must admit that it was truly a wonderful experience. The staff there is definitely doing a wonderful job with protecting the sea turtles. The deformed and blind turtles sort of made my heart sink with sorrow. This place sure needs to be on your itinerary if you plan on visiting the country.

I was not really sure about this review... Rating 5 stars a hatchery that buys turtle eggs from local fishermen that dig the sand to get those, really? Well... We took time to speak with the guy and I understand his reasons. Some locals take the turtle eggs and eat those so the hatchery buys the eggs and then releases most of the turtles in the ocean making sure they don't get eaten by birds, at least it gives those babies an additional 0.1% chance to survive. Only negative comment is that they keep (few) "adult" (~2 yo) turtles in small tanks as well as handicapped ones (fishnets, propeller, etc.)... The manager told us frankly that they need to keep some to attract people and it is also good to educate people. During one of the visit we have been able to release some babies into the sea and this was simply awesome, for the kids but for us as well !
A guided tour in the lifecycle of a turtle took us to another world...starting from the egg to a full grown turtle...and best part was touching them and lifting them in your hands..
Lovely visit with the kids being able to pick up the babies.  They are doing something fantastic and should keep up the good work.
The hatchery relies on tourists for all of its income - amazing work they are doing and a great opportunity to learn about the turtles (and have pictures, of course!!!)

I learnt so much,visiting the hatchery and seeing all the good work they do in preserving natural life in Hkkaduwa. You see the baby turtles and injured ones that are very happy in their environment , it's a real education  and they do so much good, it's quite cheap to go in and you can stay as long as you like. You may ask questions from the keepers about the turtles too. We would not have missed it and would go again when in Hikkaduwa.
Turtle farm was pretty cool.  You might want to visit several because we experience significantly different service and attention at each.

All good and definitely worth seeing - you actually get to touch the turtles. As it was very close to our hotel and we did not enjoy too much Sri Lankan driving - it was an excellent choice for quick trip.
You can visit this turtle farm with guide who will explain you everything you need to know about these sweet animals! Entrance is just 500 rupies

The owner of the turtle hutchery relates how he lost all his family to the tsunami. He carries on the hutchery by himself. He does all he can to preserve and save baby turtles who often get caught in fishermen's nets. Groups of school children come to visit and learn about turtles and their breeding habits.
Nice for The kids. Have about 9 tanks with turtles. Personly i dont like Them or others taking The turtles eggs from The beach and keep Them at The farm.

i went here to understand how sea turtles are saved from near extiction. this hatchery is well built and attracts a lot of tourists.  you need to pay certain amount of money. its a great place to learn about loggerhead turtles,  green turtles etc. they have construted water beds that shows the different growing stages of the turtles. saved turtles but disabled ones are also kep t here. overall a good place.

We did not expect our visit to the hatchery to be so interesting.  The son of the man who began it many years ago gave us a tour thoroughly explains the operation.  Although Lonely Planet seemed uncertain if such hatcheries are having a positive effect on the turtle population, we came away convinced the writers did not really understand how the hatchery operates.  I must admit I am not sure which hatchery we visited as there appear to be several in the area.  The one we went to is south of Bentota.

Turtles kept in tiny tanks, staff asking for donations to send a turtle to Europe for an operation, eggs are bought from illegal poachers and then touirists pay to see them released - Sri Lankan govt needs to police this whole nasty scene. Don't collude with it,

They buy the turtle eggs from the black market hunters for more than asking price so that these little guys don't wind up on a dinner plate. They raise the babies so that they have a 90% higher chance of survival than if they were allowed to hatch on their own in the wild. The only issue I had with this place is that the gift shop doesn't except visa.
We stopped by for a quick tour & that's all it is. It only takes about a half hour to go through the hatchery with the guide. We found it informative & a good rest stop.

We didn't know how to react to this place. We were taken there on a tour of various tourist traps and this one cost overall about as much as the others. If what we were told is true then the hatchery system seems to be a good idea and will possibly result in more wild turtles. I was amazed that the guide was blase about giving us all an egg to hold then began digging up the mounds to find a freshly hatched turtle that the kids could hold. The info on the five turtles was very interesting. However, once you move away from the hatchery area the place is extremely confronting. There are a number of extremely small, concrete,shallow square tanks with a range of larger and larger turtles that are kept permanently in sensory deprivation. It is confronting and my kids were upset by it. The 'hospital' area had a range of turtles with physical impairments that had prevented them from being released. Some of these lived permanently in buckets and washing bowls. The huge turtles damaged by the fishing industry were a sad sight to see and I do appreciate that the hatchery is likely to be doing its best for these animals. But, the enormous albino turtle, in a tank so small it can barely turn around is definitely unacceptable and is not about conservation at all. My advice, sell this poor creature to a state of the art aquarium and, if this is a serious conservation project, use the money raised to improve the standards of tanks for the 'rescue' turtles.

Very nice sancuaty to save and preserve Turtles of all species native to Sri Lanka. You get a nice guide that will explain and let you carefully hold and pet some of the newborns. You will hopefully learn somethings about the different species and how they breed and how Sri Lankas are trying to save the Tutles.

you must visit some turtles hatchery cause , its in sri lanka you can see 5 different turtles; and its nice when you touch them; and we payed 2000rps for 2p; dont forget that the turtles eat food ( fish filet) and it costs 700rps/ kg and they eat, believe me...

We had a very good time at Peraliya Sea Turtle Hatchery and the guide taught us many interesting things about the different sea turtles. We were happy to hear that most eggs nowadays are sold to the hatchery and not eaten by the locals as earlier. It's fun to hold the baby turtles and also some of the bigger ones. The turtles are hatched in the sand box, placed in tanks and then released when they reach the age of 5 (except for the injured ones that are kept and fed there for the survival of the animal). It is well worth the entrance of 500 Rs and you are also welcome to give a donation if you feel like contrubuting a bit more. The guided tour is not longer than about 15 minutes and most people seems to stay maximum 30 minutes. We truly enjoyed every minute :)

We stopped at this place while going to Galle. This is a nice place for adults and kids too. One gets an opportunity to hold baby turtles. They really do run all over the hand. Touching adult turtles is not allowed as they can bite. There are different types of turtles in the hatchery. There is also a curious handicapped turtle taken care of by the owner. One can also see a turtle egg, and how the turtles are taken care of / bred once the eggs are laid. Unfortunately we did not have anyone to explain anything to us and the person accompanying us was quite a quiet chap so we had to wriggle out answers from him. Fees are 500 Sri Lankan rupees for each person, which is a little steep is no one is going to provide any decent exploration.
This is a must visit. Shows the turtle conservatory process and the good insightful tour to learn about turtles. You get to see and hold both baby and adult turtles.

Its a cute little place opened by a buy in the memory of his family lost in tsunami. His story is explained on the all. Entrance is 500 LKR per person. On entrance you can see a small area covered in sand where eggs are kept for hatching. Then there are multiple tanks where multiple turtles in different sizes are seens. Mostly all turtles are of same type except one. They allow you to touch and old the turtles and baby turtles are so dam cute. Owner is very passionate about this place and explains about everything - how the turtles get attacked in sea n they lose a limb or so.. how he gets them thru villagers as he pays for them.

I agree with NottinghamHamble, there are 5-7 hatcheries along this stretch. I have gone through the photos and it's definitely the one we went to, with the only albino turtle. We did not pay to go in, nor were pressured to donate. Some of us did, some didn't. There WERE two shops, but again, no pressure to buy at all. Now the turtles!!!! PLUS POINTS: Loved the amount of information available, the amount of turtles & varieties as well as age ranges we saw. I didn't realise how rare the females were, which is why they keep them for longer in order to let them grow and have a better chance of survival when released. Some of these turtles would definitely have died if released into the sea. DOWNSIDE: We really should have been asked to wash our hands on arrival. There is a big sign saying don't touch the albino as it's immune system is weaker, yet we are wearing sun creams, make up, moisturisers, perfumes etc, etc. How about all the others that we've dipped our hands into?! We should really have been offered to rinse our hands on entry as well as on departure!!! Some of the tanks are a little small,but hey, they are still trying to recover so many years after the tsunami. WELL worth the visit though, very educational too.

Nice for the kids to hold the baby turtles. They had a lot of fun. I'm not 100% sure of the legitimacy of the place, as in, does it look after the turtles, or does it keep them just to get paying turtles to visit?

The small Hutchery is excellent! best experience to pat a little turtle! the owner explained a lot about the sea turtles and the 500 RS. were a good spend to help the place and there work. extremely recommended!

500 rupees to get in. The owner is very passionate about his work and seems to be doing a good job. As others noted, hard to tell if it's conservation or money making - but I lean towards conservation. Owner buys eggs dug up by locals and hatches and releases most. a handful are kept in the tanks. was surprised how "cute" the turtles were, including larger ones. Beautiful shells which they seemed to enjoy us tickling. Our kids got to hold baby turtles. Only takes about 30 minutes but overall worthwhile checking out. We added in the photo museum re Tsunami to make a mini half day tour out of.
A good example of sustainable conservation. What started off as a small hatchery sometime ago, now attracts many visitors.

Fun half an hour - very small so you see it all quickly. You get to hold baby turtles who are very cute (and some of the bigger ones!). It's meant to be a sanctuary but I guess you don't really know if it does help turtles or it's a money making scheme to get tourists cash. No way of telling really. But it is an enjoyable 30 mins and very cheap. When we were there the owner who gave us the tour didn't try to sell us any other additions - he told us his story which was very sad (family killed in the tsunami) but was polite and informative on the turtles.

We went there with our kids, they really liked it and also we contributed to a good cause which feels like a win win. Nice to see all the beautiful turtles and the beautiful work that they are doing for the eco system in Sri Lanka.

the reviews below are a bit confusing because there are a number of hatcheries, some more business orientated than others. The original hatchery is at Kosgoda. The owner pays local people for the eggs to prevent them being sold for food illegally. they are then re-buried until they hatch and then kept in tanks until their release, 4 weeks later, when they stand a better chance of surviving. You will see hnewly hatched turtles, the egg beds, Oliver Ridley, Hawksbill, Loggerhead and Green turtles. The aim is to release them. Well worth paying the money to support such a cause. There is nothing for sale here (no gem shop or people pursuading you to part with more money). A 45 min bus ride from Hikkaduwa (30p!) which is an experience in itself (or go by Tuk Tuk)
we so very cute turtles and especially the small ones were so cute.. you can experience and get to know more facts about turtles from this place..   XO XO

We visited one turtle hatchery near to Kosgoda on our half-day trip by tuk-tuk to maddu river safari. Entry is 500 LKR per person. The guide explained and showed various type of turtles in different stages of their lifecycles and you can hold the turtles in your hands and take photos. Overall a good half an hour of experience - recommended.

The turtle hatchery was interesting in that you were able to pick up the turtles so that you could be photographed with them and the owner provided some really interesting facts about turtles and conservation efforts. I also do somewhat agree with some of the criticisms that the tanks seemed small and the owner was doing a good job of trying to get more money out of tourists after you paid the admission to get in. Theres a sign asking for donations for other costs and you can also pay to buy and release a baby turtle into the ocean. I'm hoping the money is going to the purpose stated and there is a lot of good being done here. All that being said I do feel it's at least worth a visit.

I liked playing with the turtles and taking photos and that the people there are taking care for 10 years even for the turtles which they are hurt and disabled. I disliked that they employees are begging for donation saying sad stories that it just ruin you vacation mood. Anyhow people are giving donations ant tips, so there is no need to extort money from them. Anyhow it was worth the visit.
a very nice place to get to know about sea turtles. the guys teach you and also lets you to touch the little ones..  nice experience..   totally worth it.
These people are trying to help the turtle population to grow back. Visit them is a cool experience and moreover you support their environmental-friendly activities. Go there if u have the chance!
Worth a visit, but to expensive to recommend. We didnt see the nightlife of the turtles, but during days, its just ok,

the children were totally fascinated by the turtles, seeing the illustrations of the life cycle (hatching eggs), and the different pools for different sized turtles. I personally couldn't help escape the feeling that something got rather lost in translation and felt unsure if it truly was a sanctuary or a business opportunity

there are many hutchery and they are privately owned your guide keeps commission in your visit charge being the follower of buddhism , remember u can offer tips to guides or helper as per ur wish, they will accept anything

I wouldn't call this a sanctuary, maybe more a zoo. I'm disappointed in this place, but there has been 'poor/terrible' reviews on TripAdvisor so I knew what to expect. I'm not sure if I regret paying the entry, but I didn't make a donation, I definitely felt scammed with the owner asking for more money. The turtles are not a pleasant environment, however they are been protected from becoming a local meal or decoration, so then maybe this place is doing its job. I'm sorry this review isn't more definitive, I don't know whether tourists should be supporting this type of operation or not. It shows how hard it is to do ecotourism the right way. If you do decide to go, you need 20 mins max here. The turtles are just wallowing in shallow concrete pools. There is a mixture of just hatched babies (hatchlings?), not yet fully grown adults (this seems the most cruel, in the owners words they are kept only for tourists to be able to see a bigger size turtle, rather than released, shame on the owner) and injured adults (which makes the most sense been in captivity).

This place was advised to me by the hotel owner where I stayed. I am glad that I took the opportunity to visit as it was very interesting and educational. I would recommend that anyone visit this place regardless of age, gender etc.
Somebody wants to make money here. Poor turtles. Please don t support these people by taking money to them.

And this can either be a hit or a miss with people going by some of the negative comments on here, we arrived with an open mind especially after I had been swimming with green turtles in the wild in Hawaii the year before which was a real highlight for me personally, and to be honest anybody who releases turtles back into the wild gets my vote any day. When you consider just how threatened they've become, and they are still being trapped and killed by local fisherman mainly Tamils & Muslims for food however, the Buddhist Sri Lankan's tend to view them differently and do their best to bring any injured turtles in to places like this along with the many eggs that are laid along the beaches for a small fee in return of course, I think it's around 30 Rupees an egg and everyone's a winner here.? You will pay 500 Rupees each to enter which is a couple of Pounds or around three Dollars and won't break the bank either, I have to admit this place was smaller than I expected and the tanks holding the bigger turtles looked inadequate too. However, walking around with a young lady who also seemed pretty knowledgeable and explained the work that they do, even telling me we couldn't touch any baby turtles due to the risk of infecting them, now to my amazement I watched some Dutch people handling them which was a contradiction in it's self as I pointed out. There is also a large turtle with three flippers which can never be released into the wild and I was told later it's been in that small tank for years, perhaps a bigger tank would be a good idea ?  Looking at the baby turtles we were told they're released after three months to give them a fighting chance in the wild which is a good idea and as we were staying just along the road it was easy to jump in a Tuk, Tuk, and come back in the evening, along with a small donation we got to release some baby turtles into the surf, a real magical moment indeed and one to remember. We also got to meet the owner and he did seem a genuine guy who also took time to explain a few things to us, the downside here is the aforementioned Gem shop attached to the hatchery with a seedy guy trying to entice you in to look at his overpriced tat.  I can only assume he's sharing the ground rent or something?  He has nothing to do with the turtles thankfully, also do remember there are dozens of "Hatcheries" up and down the coast here some good, some bad. One we went to later asked us for a donation of 10,000 Rupees to release ONE TURTLE..!  That's around £50 in my money needless to say he was politely told where to go, so be warned.! As for this hatchery I would recommend a visit especially for kids, and yes we all know it's geared for tourists but, just keep an open mind and for a small donation a once in a lifetime opportunity exists to release some turtles and make a small difference to the planet, which only a short while ago had uneducated, smiling, dumb tourists standing on beaches around the World watching a turtle being killed by locals and cooked in it's own shell before being served up as a beach dinner, thankfully people are better educated in environmental issues these days..!
if youve been to kenya youll see the diffrence , the staff where just going through the motion there was no passion

I took my 3 year old son to have a look at the turtles and he loved the experience. It is nice to see the work that they do and you get to hold some of the small turtles. It is good for a short visit and it fairly small but if you are in Hikkaduwa then definitely worth checking out.
If you have 30 minutes, this is a worthwhile stop. Got to see...and in some cases touch...several turtles at the hatchery that had been injured and would not have survived in the wild.

They told us it was good for the turtles but I was not convinced. They would dig up eggs laid by turtles and make them hatch in the hatcheries and later release the turtles back in the sea except for the ones which are injured. I was not sure if interfering with the natural birthing is helpful or not
Nice to hold the turtles and learn a little. They will ask you for a donation at the end - be prepared.
Doesn't take long, great experience and you get to learn about them as well as understand the amazing conservation work he is running. 500 entry and can give donations, can stay as long as you want.
did that as a part of the lagoon tour. The hutchery is not that big but nice enough to see. Walking distance from city.

We went en-route to the mangrove boat trip and whilst it is good the work they do and the guy taking us round explaining stuff was good, it is done and dusted within half an hour. It is worth a visit cos you have to really if your in the local area. I wouldn't travel miles and miles just for the turtle hatchery though. Items in the gift shop are very expensive. I believe entrance is about 500 rupee which is a couple of quid or so, so it isn't gonna break the bank. If you want to feed a big turtle though, head to hotel Traaya Tranz in Hikkaduwa. Go onto the beach at about 9am and you will be able to feed a huge Green Turtle which comes in daily. You will get total close up photos and be able to rub sand on its shell and feed it seaweed. If you find this review helpful please give me a helpful tick. Jamie of wisbech
Really lovely. Had a guide explaining all to us. As I remember quite expensive to get in and then at the end of the tour you feel pressured to donate more money to the trust fund.

OK, you've got to like turtles, but who doesn't. Recently hatched turtles waiting to be released into the sea, plus some larger wounded ones in turtle hospital. A nice story, although some of the tanks are clearly too small.

Worried that this is a scam, but hope I'm wrong. 500 rupees by Sri Lanka standards is expensive. Would like to hear from visitors who have seen the turtles being released. Is there a timetable showing this? I'm no expert, but feel that multiple visitors covered with oil and sunscreen, picking up turtles to pose for photographs, can do them little good. Great photo opportunities, but far more exciting to see them swimming close to shore off the beach. We saw many in this area while dining at the JLH Beach Front Restaurant.

This place is wonderful if you want to learn about turtles. It's about 25 mins out of Hikkaduwa and down a long driveway, (There is a hatchery closer,) The gentleman running the place was keen to show us the different turtles, new hatchlings as well as older turtles which will remain at the hatchery. You are able to hold them with supervision. Great experience and worthy cause.
We have been here on 20 August 2014. Good explanations from the british volunteer. Our children enjoyed the place very much

We paid 1500 indian rupees for a family of 5 (3 kids). We got a good detailed explanation from the gentleman who runs the place. Kids were given a chance to handle the little turtles and they loved it!! It just took 45 mts for us to be done with this, but our kids recollect as if we spent the whole day!!
the man running this place was really nice and helpful. im glad to see the help that can be done. plenty of information written as well.

I loved it here j Just a little shack on the beach but doing an amazing job and u can see and hold baby turtles Lots of other turtles maimed by fishing nets which is really sad but at least they have somewhere to live

we were initially surprised at the SLK500 entrance fee but once we saw the good work being done we were very happy to have contributed. There were eggs hatching and we were able to take them out of the sand and place in the tanks. The guide who took us around was well informed and we found it to be very educational and an exellent conservation project.    EK Amarasena Fernendo near the saw mill  Welipara

Well, the story goes that the owner lost his family and the hatchery in the Tsunami.  I hope that isn't all true but many people did die here.  Unfortunately, after multiple visits and many rupees to enter and for donation (turtle food?) I do feel like the place is a scam.  Nothing changes.  He has the same "rescued" turtles and just as many baby turtles as every other day.   I am very unsure as to how legit these places are.

OK it initially seems like a turtle petting zoo BUT there is a method to the madness and they claim to have returned over 10,000 turtles to the wild based on our donations and entry fees. That seems a job well done, right? You might like to see it done differently BUT they are trying and they should be applauded for it. If you have kids its a winner, a real winner. On the strength of this visit we went to another sanctuary further north (40 Mins) and this was a bigger version of the same again worth a visit.
Small hatchery not far from the beach. The staff is very knowledgable and the turtles are insanely adorable.

the place is fairly simple and rather primitive, but it is worth the visit to understand' appreciate and support the voluntary mission that that local environmentalists took upon themselves to preserve the local sea turtles, that would have been otherwise eliminated. the turtles life cycle is fully demonstrated and one appreciates their willing to hold invalid turtles in special tanks till they die.
Its a small place, you get done in an hour but worth learning lifecycles of sea turtles, seeing them, holding baby turtles, understanding their habitat etc, worth it if you like animals.

We visited this place all the way from Unawatuna and the visit was worth a trip. We were quite amazed with the enthusiam the owners and workers have. We had a brief session by the owner & founder of the place with the activities conducted by the hatchery. We had the opputunity to hold the small to large turtles. Highly recommended.

Arranged by our hotel - a 40 minute tuk-tuk ride north along the coast road. Lots of turtles which you can hold - pay the extra in advance and arrange to do a release, which is a truly magical experience!

Really nice place to see! This people help the Turtle population grow and do a great job! Nice that they give information about what they exactly do too. They have a nice souvenier shop aswell. Also remarkable to see how they build back their hatchery after the tsunami destroyed it all. Deffinatly worth a visit!
Nice place to see how people are caring about turtles! Amazing to see the small turtles of 1-3 days!
Great little excursion. We took our kids back in the evening to help release the young turtles into the sea.

It's a basic premise and it doesn't matter whether you buy all the stories etc because... the turtles are SO cute! Plus this one is really conveniently located. So we ended up spending ages handling the baby turtles and had to drag ourselves away. V popular with a small child (although we drew the line at the guy's offer to actually get into the tank with the turtles!)

To start with there are a lot of turtle farms on the way to Colombo, I guess most of them are same.   Although the entry fees is on the higher side, its worth it because you can interact with the turtle very closely.  Its also a learning experience to know about this endangered species.  A guide tells you all the info on the turtles There were quiet a lot them the hatchery we visited in various tanks.  We as adults enjoyed it a lot. If you going there with children I guess they would have lot more fun holding these tiny turtle (and few big ones too). There is a souvenir shop too
It was lovely to see the eggs and baby turtles which are put back in the sea. Not so sure about the fully grown ones in small tanks.

It was great! The baby turtles were so cute I got to hold one. If u are a turtle lover u have got to come here! Tonight I'm going to release some baby turtles! (This review written by my 8 yo daughter- the man who runs this is a true gem- it's free but we left a donation to help him feed and help the turtles. Go here. Learn about the turtles and his history which is quite sad however he has risen above a lot :)
You can see and touch a lot of turtles, new-born and a very old ones there. The owner will tell you stories of each of his pets :)

We visited the turtle hatchery on the way to Galle. They do a fantastic job there. The fishermen sell the turtle eggs to them and they keep them and let them hatch. They are very caring and have some old and also injured turtles there. They let us hold a baby turtle that had just hatched and we put it in the water so it could swim.
We like that it was an informative type of event.  We learned so much about the community's effort to preserve these adorable creatures.  if you have time - worth a visit!

We went to one of the many turtle hatcheries along the West coast of Sri Lanka between Colombo and Galle. Entry ticket was 4 USD/person. We reached at about 11am and spent an hour and half understanding the conservation efforts being put in by the various groups. Thousands of baby turtles swam around in concrete tanks. We're told some of them had hatched that morning, about 5hr ago. We were allowed to hold the baby turtles and pose for photographs. Among the 20 or so big turtles, a rare albino turtle was told to be 200+ year old. Must visit if you're in SL for a leisure trip

It was just concrete tanks with turtles of varying age and deformaties. We visited the turtles as part of a day trip to Galle,Moon stone mine and river boat ride all three more interesting than the turtles.

We went as they were closing, but they were very happy to open-up and show us their good works.  It was an impressive endeavour.   It is managed on a very low budget and we were happy to contribute in a very small way to the welfare of these endangered species.   It was all very scientifically run with clutches of eggs all marked-out in the sand hatcheries.   Then the hatchlings are cared for a few extra days than normal so that their umbilical cord (from the egg sack) can heal.  This, along with human release into the  sea (which you can do yourself) hugely enhances the turtles' chances of survival.  A great place to visit.

The man has to buy the turtle eggs from the markets, as apparently the locals dig them up to eat, ( as they are considered to increase male libido). He then hatches them and release them back to the sea. So, the SLR500pp although expensive is worth it IMHO. He also asked for an additional donation telling us all of his family died in the 2004tsunami. It sucked my husband in, and he gave another large amount of money.

Interesting place to visit and good explanation of turtles from the staff. Visitin the afternnon around 5pm as you might have the option to help releasing small turtles into the sea if you give a donation.

Visited Turtle Hatchery for an hour. Tickets is 500 rupees (4 dollars), seems expensive for such  a short visit. Great enjoyment for kids. Many turtles. The biggest is 15 kg weight, really heavy. Baby turtle is good for my kids. Got good explanation from the owner. Nice place.
Fascinating story about the turtles lives and the work people do to keep the baby turtle safe until it is released out into the ocean.

The entrance fee/donation of Rs.500 per person seems a bit steep for this small attraction, but how often do you get to play with baby turtles and even hold a grown olive ridley? All of the turtles are kept in concrete enclosures with water for them to swim in. The owner tells you how his family was killed in the Tsunami and tries to get extra donation from you. But he doesn't push it and is very subtle about it. You can contribute if you wish but otherwise just play with the turtles and leave.
Interesting but I was distressed to see how small and barren the tanks were for their long stay residents.

Very educational and most informative. A must if you go to Hikkaduwa. Gives a real feeling that there is a definite effort being made for conservation. Well worth the visit. Larry & Ashlee P. ( Melbourne- Australia)

Visited the hatchery early in the morning and received a one to one experience with turtles hatching in our hands. Its says donations welcomed but there is a charge of 500 rupees (about £2.50) to go in. Excellent value for money and the whole visit will not last longer than 30 minutes. Many critical comments about this place, but I see it as no different to UK Animal sanctuarys that are struggling to break even

It's a small little place, and whilst learning the story of the turtles is nice if you have a guide, I paid 500rupees at the door and really it was probably more of a token gesture as I went in for around 3 minutes, looked around and was done. Not worth a huge trip if you're going massively out your way but if you're passing, then sure, why not pop in. Just don't expect too much. The baby turtles are cute though.

Seeing on the entrance ticket they ask and what get inside is not worth for money. I am a budget traveler, If you have time and money then you can plan a visit to the place. Its nothing just like a turtle zoo. I think better you put your money in a zoo where for the same price you will be able to see more animals..this is my own personal opinion.

Nice to see the turtles and the eggs BUT..... 15 minute visit, in and out, they want the donations, not very nice conditions, dirty water, I would try and find a more professional establishment elsewhere on the island, rather than a shack on the beach.

Entrance is 500 rupees and well worth it. You see some incredible species of turtles and see how they are cared for. the family owner Santha loves his turtles and during the Tsunami he went back to save them after making sure that his family ere not in danger. Many tourists donate to this good cause to help safeguard and look after the turtles. This hatchery was in Welipara, Hiddarura
The one we went to was in Galle, I understand there is one in Hikkaduwa, but it was nice and the people seem to care, and it is only 400 rupees (€2.50)

The operator is saving turtle eggs from being sold as food, hatching them, and releasing them.  He also provides hospice & hospital care to older/injured turtles.  Children are able to see turtles up close, and to see baby turtles swimming in tanks.  Definitely worth supporting.
I am from India. Have seen plenty of turtle hatchery. Max 30 min in and out. Can visit if you have time to kill. They are more keen on additional donation.
Enjoyed seeing this a lot. Well worth the trip...a highlight. Loved the albino turtles. My son is still talking about this.
It was good to see the turtle hatchery. there were not many turtles But the fact that you can pick them and can see them really close. It was good.
A bit focused on donations, and it is quite small. But it is cool to see and hold the tiny turtles, and to look at the older, unfortunate turtles. In and out in 10-15 min.

I can't speak with any authority as I'm not a naturalist but this place just seemed to be a grubby tourist trap which makes money out of appearing to be supporting the animals. They were all kept in crowded small tanks. The only thing the owner was interested in was getting our money. Their website says they are 'non-profit' but that frankly could mean anything. Apart from anything else it is basically someone's backyard with about 8 concrete tanks. That's it. The main attraction seems to be that you can pick up the baby turtles but (again I am not a nauralist)  I can't imagine that's much good for them - being picked up by hundreds of tourists covered in germs. Avoid.
You are able to hold the baby turtles and get up close with bigger turtles. Learned some interesting turtle trivia.
I got to hold a 3-day all turtle. This place needs to be supported; they save injured turtles and help the hatchlings survive. The best thing about Hikkaduwa.
You will be in and out within 45 min but the kids loved being able to hold the baby turtles. Good guides and info.

but nothing to write home about.  We saw the turtles & that was it really, in & out in probably less than 10 minutes.  A donation was mentioned but as much as we'd love to, we simply cannot afford to keep donating.  Maybe I caught them on a bad day, or perhaps this is only something that would appeal to kids, or people with kids.
The sheer pleasure of holding day-old or week-old turtle babies in the hand is something completely unforgettable experience. A must-visit spot

This was an interesting place and obviously performing an important role in saving turtle eggs from being eaten by predators including human beings. The hatchery is relatively primitive but that goes to its credit when it is obvious that resources are used to benefit the environment not visitors who cannot fail to be impressed by the turtle that have suffered injury and are being nursed back to health.

As other reviews have said, the turtle hatchery is a small place so you'll be in and out in 15 minutes tops although it's definitely worth a visit.  The tsunami memorial and buddha are closeby as well. There are about 6 turtles in total and you can hold an adult and baby one. Personally, I preferred seeing the wild turtles outside the Chaaya Tranz hotel, they were massive and i liked seeing them swim in the ocean more than seeing the turtles in the small enclosures at the hatchery. Be prepared for a pretty heavy sales pitch from the caretaker for an additional donation!

Was amazing to be able to hold turtle hatchlings of 1-3 days old! Fun to get up close with the different types of turtles. Nice to see turtles who are blind, disabled or unfortunate are being taken care of when they old not usually survive in the wild. Only the area of the pools they live in are very small.
it was quite interesting but small so dont expect to go and find a huge place.  it is obvious that they care for the turtles which is the most important things
We visited the oldest original turtle hatchery a bit further away (45 mins) which was great. Very interesting and lots to learn.  We could hold some of them too.
U can touch Little Turtles. They also have Turtles of different Species. They have egg hatcheries also. Nice place to visit for kiddos and adults too.
Well worth the small entry fee, great place to learn about the Turtle Cycle , good souvenir shop.  Great place to take young children.
lovely place to visit, nice to see the turtles of Hikkaduwa being looked after, they are so beautiful!

500 rupees entry fee and you get to hold baby turtles. The owner uses the money to buy turtle eggs from locals as they are seen as a delicacy in Sri Lanka. The turtles are nice to see - but it hadn't changed much since I was last here 5 years ago. I felt they could have done a better job educating visitors with displays and written information...
Worth a visit to see and hold very young turtles. Being able to hold the turtles was a lovely experience.

It was lovely to see the local community looking after the wildlife but once you had seen the turtles (and we had seen them wild in the sea the day before) there wasn't huge amount else to see. It would be nice for them to give a little more information about the project.

We arrived early one morning (9am) and it is low season. We walked in with our 3&4yr olds. The owner welcomed us instantly and advised it would be 500rupees for my wife and I (kids no charge). We paid without issue. He then showed us and talked us though each of the ponds. Giving us history on the turtles and the farm. We got to hold/take photos with turtles from 10 days old to 1.5yrs old. We were even offered a swim with one in the bigger tank! He was a really nice guy and although its small i highly reccommend! We even went back for a second time the kids loved it that much. We also left additional funds as a donation as the experience was well worth it!! I hope everyone gets the same experience we had.
Loved the idea that they were saving turtles. A little cruel as full sized sea turles were enclosed in 1.5 x 1.5 meter concrete boxes (Possibly 2x2)

We thoroughly enjoyed our visit to the Turtle hatchery, we were shown around each of the ponds and got to hold a baby turtle and also tickle a larger one.  They are obviously running the place on a small budget, there's no money wasted on fancy trimmings etc but it is doing a wonderful job of helping protect the turtles from extinction.  We weren't asked for donation or entrance fee, but were happy to buy some items from the 'gift shop' as a way of donating.

We were saddened by the story of the founders of the Turtle Hatchery. There were few big Turtles handicapped which was very sad. It is a small place with few ponds for turtles of different ages. We knew these places depended on donations so we donated few hundred rupees. While we were getting on our bike a guy walked up to us and handed us a business card, we smiled and thanks him, then he pointed out to the bottom of the card that said 500 rupees each, basically he was asking for more money, which would have been fine to pay at the entrance but sneaking up like that felt like a scam and we left feeling disappointed.

Good place to know more about turtles ,its basically for the protection of the endangered species...they have turtles from egg to the large size ones..they allow you to take the photographs if you want to

this is a very small place... and the highlight is you get to hold the just born ... found the sad story narrated by the caretaker a bit carried away ... he will ask donation for the temporary shed which is broken and the way he is struggling to maintain the place ...

We all looked this - and felt it deserved a good review for all the excellent voluntary work it does.  Pretty standard tour (small or large groups) with good english speaking guides.  A baby turtle hatched in front of our eyes, and I was given it to hold - precious!

Good to see the turtles up close and the children we saw there really seemed to enjoy it. The guides didn't really seem that interested in answering our questions and after the few tanks there's nothing else to see. If its on your way to somewhere then stop, if  not don't worry you can see them on the beach in Hikkaduwa.
A bit of a let down... Be patient on the local beaches and you'll see turtles in their natural habitat!

This is a very small venue, but turtles are big news in this part of the world, not just as a tourist attraction but also as poachers game and as a delicacy for the numerous local fish eagles. Five of the world's 7 turtle species visit SriLanka, and their breeding sites are seriously under threat. We weren't convinced that a small hatchery like this can make much difference in the overall scheme of things, but they are taking big strides in education and awareness.  Our kids are 3 & 6, and they loved it... so I suppose that's a start.  Just don't be tempted to release any of the baby turtles back to the wild during daylight hours - the fish eagles are on constant standby. We didn't much like the pressure to "donate", but we understand the need for funding. Keep up the good work

This venture is admirable. It is locally run, with minimal cost and the benefits to the turtle population are tenfold. The guides give a great explanation of the work they do and you are able to view the turtles up close and even handle the small ones. This was a great experience for adults and children alike. While we were visiting there were several school parties. The hatchery was quite crowded but groups of students very orderly. Definitely worth a visit and the 100 rupees entrance fee was very  well spent.
If you are around the Turtle Hutchery go for a short tour. Is interesting and you are learning a lot about this animal. You need only about 1 hour.

Visited this turtle hatchery last year and was impressed by the work done there. The explanations given by the owner was very informative. However on returning this year with friends, whilst the owner we saw last year was just as enthusiastic in a non forceful way, he was constantly interrupted by his brother who was asking for money to repair the roof. At the end of the visit we felt obliged to make a donation, when we asked the whereabouts of the collection box the brother asking for the money pointed to his pocket when we put the money in his pocket he immediately checked the money to see how much we had donated. It was not a please ant atmosphere. It is doubtful we will visit again
Its a nice place where you can spend time & interact with turtles. Would definitely recommend especially if you have school going kids

We loved this.  I really hope the donations are going for what they say because this place is small, but they really seem to be trying to save the turtle eggs from the soup pot.  My children got to hold the baby turtles, touch the bigger ones and feed them.  We were the only visitors at the time, and it was well worth the experience of enjoying them so up close and personal.
Small place and he ask for donation to fix roof but he has been asking for the last 4 years but never fixes it

We visited the Turtle Hatchery and hospital late one evening and were given a personal tour by the owner. They collect eggs from locals and protect them until they hatch then release them back into the Ocean at night to reduce the losses by birds. They also look after damaged turtles who would not survive in the wild. Green, Hawksbill and Olive Ridley turtles are all cared for here.
Nice to see people making a difference to the wildlife.  You can get one of the chaps at the place to give you a guided tour so you understand what they do at the hutchery.
very good place to watch. its something diffrent than the others. recommanded for all travelers should visit thi splace.
took some friends ,some hatcheries can over charge you. There are many to choose from, Don't get carried away with buying stuff that they offer, however overall the hatcheries are very interesting

We enjoyed our visit to the sanctuary and loved being able to hold a couple of the baby turtles.  We had an English speaking guide who was able to explain the work they carried out there.
