Typically, we were asked for a donation at the end which we were happy to give as we felt they were genuinely trying to increase the turtle population and were still rebuilding the sanctuary after it was virtually destroyed in the Tsunami.

We visited the turtle hatchery and were very dissapointed by the way animals were trested in tjis Place. The turtles were swimming in tiny pools made of concrete and were seemingly trying to get out there. The owner had also "rescued" a baby shark which was swimming in à tank and when we asked when it would be released he said "maybe after the tourist seasion". I didn't believe him. I was personally very disseapointed with the hatchery that claims to be rescuing turtles but is in fact just collecting money from tourists. Every chance the owner got he used to collecting more money from the tourists..and to do what? not to improve the hatchery at least. We even heard from à local contact who is working in the Sri lankan environmental department that the whole business of the hatcheries buying turtle eggs is not to help the turtles since apparently the baby turtles only have energy to swim into the Middle of the ocean directly when they come out of their eggs...at the hatchery the babies are kept in the pool for days without food and when eventuelly they are released only à tiny percentage of them has the energy left to swim and not get eaten by fish directly. Therefore, the hatchery is in fact reducing the chances of the turtles since locals now go and find eggs they can sell to the hatchery. The environmental Department Worker also Said the shark the owner is keeping is endangered and illegal to keep as a pet. Seriously, if you care about turtles tjis is not the business to support. I hope the environmental Department is able to shut tjis Place down.

It's a really good place to visit if you like turtles. The place and facilities are not really outstanding and I think need some renovations. They have different turtles that they rescued. It was a really nice experience to hold small turtles. The staff seemed pretty friendly and eager to tell about all the turtles. I think it's a place worth visiting.
Definitely worth a visit if you are in the area.  The Tsunami memorial and museum are also very close

We visited the hutchery recently and were shown around by one of the staff members who spoke good english. We held turtle eggs and baby turtles, and one larger turtle. They explain the work they do in assisting the turtle population. It is interesting and seems to be a good cause. It will not take you a long time to visit as it is only a small place, but it is a nice experience.

This is a good place to visit if you like to sea rescued turtles. I didn't think that the facility was all that inspiring in terms of visitor information or setup but it was still cool to see the turtles and to at least believe that something was being done to help save them.

Second sanctuary I have visited in Sri Lanka and I am always left wondering if they are really above board, worthy places or just tourist attractons? Both places have the "one in a million" albino turtle that would not cope in the ocean so it is therefore kept in captivity for its own safety. They were very concious about cross contamination which was good to see but the general conditions were not the most professional. If they do what they say they do then all the best but if you are a real animal lover it might be worth doing more investigation before your visit.
It is quiet an experience holding the tiny baby turtles. Saw other turtles that were rescued. Truly worth it!
They're doing great work here. The staff were enthusiastic and keen to share their knowledge and experience about their conservation work.

The hatchery is located just outside the town of Hikkaduwa and is quite small, there are a number of small water pools with turtles that have been rescued from fishing nets, many are injured and seemed to be in good care. Like everything else in Sri Lanka the establishment is rundown and in need of a cash infusion. However, I thought the care given the turtles was as good as can be expected, you are allowed to touch and handle the turtles. My big disparagement was that I wanted to release the baby turtles into the ocean however there were no eggs close to being hatched and the owner agreed to call me when ready(3-4 days), well I waited a week and the call never came, still a worthwhile visit.
very poor doesnt worth it, they tell its the bigest one in sri lanka and it looks like an ugly backyard. if we knew its that poor we wouldn't go.
U need a good guide inside, we had a french volunteer who supported us with so much passion, it was wonderful.
while it is small and poorly funded the intention is good. The feeling one gets when releasing a baby turtle is special.

This is the second visit to the turtle sanctuary - once before the tsunami and once in the new complex. You get to handle day old baby turtles and get an informed guide who describes the process of incubating the turtle eggs, hatching the eggs and, when old enough, releasing the baby turtles to the ocean. They also have older turtles which, again, you can handle. A very worthwhile venue to visit and an opportunity gorgeous spectacular photos if turtles.
It was just All in All a perfect couple of hours, especially when you have kids!!! We came a little late, they set out the turtles a 1830, but then the owner took us after to set some free:-)
I had never been to a turtle hutchery,  We all learned a lot and would recommend others to take advantage of this opportunity if in the area.

We watched this in Northern Cypress and these guys need a medal just as they all do. As if they haven't got enough on their plates because they are still suffering somewhat, 7 years after the terrible Tsunami.

You help nature by visiting this place. They don't catch wild life for human amusement. They keep wounded turtles and release hatch 3 days old turtles to he see in a safer way then what nature normally provides them.
great to see (and hold) the 2-3 day old turtles getting ready to be released!!   Also to compare with adolescent and adults and to learn about these beautiful creatures.

We had booked a trip to go there however the trip decided to pick us up AFTER going there so we went in a taxi instead. We arrived and we were able to hold tiny 1day old turtles and the purred if you stroked their heads. I also held a larger turtle. Without us going there the place wouldnt stay open as it is purely funded by visitors. I would highlylrecommend going as you can be hands on better then a zoo, its cheap to get to by taxi and its in the shade.

A small ride from central areas and a small setup, this was a great way to spend 800Rs. and a couple hours. The lady behind the cash box spoke English fairly well and guided us around the few cement tanks to show us babies that had just hatched, rescued/recovering turtles, adults soon to be released and endangered species. She even picked up different turtles (twice the size of a dinner plate) and let us hold it/take pictures with it. We got to craddle the babies and learn about their life span/enviroment and issues facing these creatures. It did not feel like a tourist trap or a terrible cash grab, a majority of the funds go back to helping save the turtles from poachers/extinction.

Great to see some good conservation work going on here!  Great to see tiny turtle babies and you can hold one too if you want.  Amazing to see how much stronger they get in just a few days. There were also some injured turtles kept permanently at the hatchery.  I felt pretty sad to see them as their pools a really quite small but they would die very quickly in the wild.

We were briefed about the turtles and their details and a bit of the history of the place and shown different types of turtles at different ages. My little one wanted to stay more time with the 1-2 days old turtle pond. It was pretty amazing a big bunch of 1 day old turtles swimming around. And ticket was just 30 rupees for locals and it is very cheap.
It's very interesting to learn about their project and to see the mini turtels being only 1, 2 or 3 days old in their pools.

Great information about the life cycle of turtles and brilliant visuals of turtles being able to handle a number of varieties of turtle is great. The baby turtles are a real blast and an absolute kids magnet - awesome. Disagree with shoppers beware - yes there is a little pressure to buy but a polite no thanks gets you out the door with no regret - you pay to enter so no guilt either.

Worth a visit as the guide will tell you this is funded only by tourists money. It takes about 15 mins to be guided around and then your in their shop with lots of cute turtle stuff. However the price is sometimes as much as 50x more than in the shop. If you buy remember its over priced and the extra money is supposed to be going to the up keep of the place. Also don't be rushed around you have paid the  entrance fee so take your time it's really interesting, we gave a donation in the box in the shop as didn't feel right paying over the odds for the stuff in shop.

This place is quite interesting..simply liked, we went in a group of 15 and was amazed to see turtle eggs, they were small and seemed like table tennis ball. guide are pretty excellent.Should visit this place at night time when they leave turtle in the sea.
